summary:
This is the paper that proves the global Langlands correspondence in the “automorphic to Galois” direction for every connected reductive group over a global function field. Let X be a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over F_q with function field F, G reductive over F, N ⊂ X a finite subscheme, K_N the associated level subgroup and Ξ ⊂ Z(F)\\Z(A) a lattice. Théorème 11.11 (split case) and Théorème 12.3 (general case) give a **canonical** decomposition of the space of cuspidal automorphic forms C^{cusp}_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, Q̄_ℓ) = ⊕_σ H_σ indexed by global Langlands parameters — Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugacy classes of continuous semisimple σ : Gal(F̄/F) → ^LG(Q̄_ℓ) unramified outside N — compatible with the Satake isomorphism at every unramified place and with the limit over N. The article is completely independent of the Arthur–Selberg trace formula. It rests on two ingredients: the moduli of shtukas, introduced by Drinfeld for GL_r and generalized to reductive groups by Varshavsky, and the geometric Satake equivalence of Lusztig, Drinfeld, Ginzburg and Mirković–Vilonen.

The mechanism is this. For every finite set I and every representation W of (Ĝ)^I there is a stack Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W} of shtukas with legs (x_i)_{i∈I} — the intersection of a Hecke stack with the graph of the Frobenius of Bun_{G,N} — which plays the role of a Shimura variety but exists for every I and every W, not only for a minuscule coweight. Its degree-zero compactly supported cohomology, H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W}, is a functor in W on (X ∖ N)^I, carries commuting partial Frobenius morphisms and Hecke operators, and is compatible with the coalescence of legs (Théorème 1.17 c), Proposition 4.12). Creation and annihilation morphisms attached to Ĝ-invariant vectors x ∈ W and ξ ∈ W^* let one write the unramified Hecke operator T(h_{V,v}) as create two legs at v → apply the partial Frobenius → annihilate (Proposition 6.2), which extends every Hecke operator to all of (X ∖ N)^I (Corollaire 6.5) and yields the **Eichler–Shimura relations** (Proposition 7.1): the partial Frobenius at a leg is killed by a polynomial in the Hecke operators, by a tensor-algebra argument modelled on a proof of Cayley–Hamilton. Those relations make the **Hecke-finite** part of the cohomology a union of constructible subsheaves stable under the partial Frobenius (Proposition 8.27), so **Drinfeld’s lemma** applies and gives it an action of Gal(F̄/F)^I; the specialization map identifies the fibre at Δ(η̄) with the one at η̄^I (Corollaire 8.34). The resulting spaces H_{I,W} form a functor in W with coalescence isomorphisms and H_{∅,1} = C^{cusp}_c (Proposition 9.7) — the last equality because Hecke-finite = cuspidal (Proposition 8.23).

From these three properties alone the **excursion operators** S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} are built: create legs at one generic point, let Galois move them around the curve independently, bring them back, annihilate. They generate a commutative algebra B, depend only on the invariant function f ∈ O(Ĝ\\(Ĝ)^I/Ĝ) attached to (W, x, ξ), satisfy explicit relations (Lemme 10.1, Proposition 10.8), are continuous, contain the unramified Hecke operators (Lemme 10.2) and are unramified outside N (Proposition 10.10, found by Böckle, Harris, Khare and Thorne). Spectral decomposition of B gives a decomposition into generalized eigenspaces — B is not known to be reduced, so simultaneous diagonalization is not available — and Proposition 11.7 turns each character of B into a semisimple parameter σ, unique up to conjugacy, using Richardson’s theorem that a tuple has a closed diagonal conjugation orbit exactly when it is semisimple.

§12 redoes everything for non-split G, with parahoric Bruhat–Tits models, the twisted geometric Satake equivalence, the L-group, and Bun_{G,N}(F_q) as a ker^1(F, G)-indexed union of adelic quotients for inner forms; §13 obtains the same decomposition with F̄_ℓ-coefficients; §14 sketches the metaplectic case; §15 relates the excursion operators to geometric Langlands; §16 shows how the theorem reproves the recursion ingredient of Laurent Lafforgue’s theorem for GL_r. Conjectures 12.7 and 12.12 state what is expected and unproved: that the parameters come from elliptic Arthur parameters, and that the decomposition is motivic and independent of ℓ.

items.name: Theorem 11.11 (= Theorem 0.1): the canonical decomposition of cuspidal automorphic forms by global Langlands parameters
items.statement: Let X be a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over F_q with function field F, G a split connected reductive group over F, N ⊂ X a finite subscheme with level subgroup K_N = Ker(G(O) → G(O_N)), and Ξ ⊂ Z(F)\Z(A) a lattice. Then there is a canonical decomposition of C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, Q̄_ℓ)-modules C^{cusp}_c(G(F)\G(A)/K_NΞ, Q̄_ℓ) = ⊕_σ H_σ, the sum being indexed by global Langlands parameters — Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugacy classes of morphisms σ : Gal(F̄/F) → Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ), defined over a finite extension of Q_ℓ, continuous, semisimple and unramified outside N. It is characterized by H_σ = H_ν for the character ν of the excursion algebra B given by ν(S_{I,f,(γ_i)_{i∈I}}) = f((σ(γ_i))_{i∈I}); it is compatible with the Satake isomorphism at every place v of X ∖ N, and with the limit over N.
items.locator: Théorème 11.11, p. 148 (§11.3); stated as Théorème 0.1, p. 2, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans exactly this: "Establish the canonical decomposition of the fixed-level cuspidal space, unramified Satake compatibility and independence from auxiliary leg choices", with this paper named as its source. The theorem is the "automorphic to Galois" direction only; Arthur multiplicity formulas are explicitly out of reach of these methods (p. 3).

items.name: Theorem 12.3: the decomposition for groups that need not be split
items.statement: For G a connected reductive group over F, not necessarily split, the same conclusion holds with the left-hand side replaced by a direct sum, indexed by ker^1(F, G) = Ker(H^1(F, G) → ∏_v H^1(F_v, G)), of spaces of cuspidal automorphic forms for inner forms of G, and with the Langlands parameters σ defined through the L-group: continuous semisimple morphisms Gal(F̄/F) → ^LG(Q̄_ℓ) = Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ) ⋊ Gal(F̄/F) whose projection to Gal(F̄/F) is the identity, taken up to Ĝ(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugacy, unramified outside N. Passing to the limit over N (Remarque 12.4) gives a canonical decomposition of the cuspidal representation of G(A) indexed by Langlands parameters.
items.locator: Théorème 12.3, p. 151, with Remarques 12.2 and 12.4, pp. 150, 152, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "For nonsplit G include the projection to the Galois group and conjugacy convention"; GS.0 plans "the adelic description of rational points in the appropriate torsor classes rather than identifying the entire stack with one double quotient", which is exactly the ker^1(F, G)-indexed sum (Remarque 12.2); RG2.5 owns the L-group with its projection and action law.

items.name: Proposition 0.41 and Proposition 10.10: unramifiedness and compatibility with the Satake isomorphism
items.statement: Every σ occurring in the decomposition is unramified at every place v of X ∖ N, and for every irreducible representation V of Ĝ the Hecke operator T(h_{V,v}) acts on H_σ by the scalar χ_V(σ(Frob_v)), χ_V the character of V and Frob_v any lift of a Frobenius element at v. The unramifiedness comes from the fact that the creation morphisms are morphisms of sheaves on all of ∆(X ∖ N), so S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_iδ_i)} for δ_i in the inertia I_v; Proposition 10.10 (found by Böckle, Harris, Khare and Thorne) is the stronger statement that S_{I,f,(γ_i)_{i∈I}} depends only on the image of (γ_i)_{i∈I} in π_1(X ∖ N, η)^I. The proof of the Satake compatibility uses that Hecke operators at unramified places are diagonalizable, being normal operators on the hermitian space of C-valued cuspidal forms.
items.locator: Proposition 0.41 and Lemme 0.38, pp. 34–36; Proposition 10.10, p. 140, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "unramified Satake compatibility"; its acceptance test "unramified GL_n matches characteristic polynomials" is this statement. Proposition 10.10 is used in Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne [BHKT16], which is PAPER job #1468 in this repository.

items.name: Remark 1.1 and Definition 1.2: π_0(Bun_G), and the Hecke stacks with bounded relative position
items.statement: Remarque 1.1 ([BD99], [Var04, lemme 2.2]): π_0(Bun_G) is canonically π_1(G) = X_*(T)/X_*(T^{sc}), which is canonically the character group of Z_Ĝ; [ω] denotes the class of a coweight. Definition 1.2: for a finite set I, an ordered partition (I_1, …, I_k) and a finite N ⊂ X, Hecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} classifies points x_i ∈ (X ∖ N)(S), objects (G_0, ψ_0), …, (G_k, ψ_k) of Bun_{G,N}(S), and isomorphisms φ_j away from ∪_{i∈I_j}Γ_{x_i} respecting the level structures; for an I-tuple ω̱ of dominant coweights, Hecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,≲ω̱} is the closed substack cut out by the weak bound φ_j((G_{j−1})_{V_λ}) ⊂ (G_j)_{V_λ}(Σ_{i∈I_j}⟨λ, ω_i⟩Γ_{x_i}) for every dominant weight λ, and by [Var04, lemme 3.1] it is an algebraic stack locally of finite type. The stack depends on the *order* of the parts, and joining parts with adjacent indices gives the forgetful morphisms π^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{(I′_1,…,I′_{k′})} (Remarque 1.4); truncations are taken by the Harder–Narasimhan polygon of G_0 (Notation 1.5) precisely because those are the ones the forgetful morphisms preserve.
items.locator: Remarques 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, Définition 1.2 and Notation 1.5, pp. 42–43, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.1 plans the bounded Hecke stacks. **Remarque 1.3 records a defect in the literature**: the author says that condition iii′)_ω̱ of [Var04, définition 2.4] — which also appeared in arXiv versions 1–3 of this paper — "probably did not give the right definition of Hecke_{N,I,ω̱} (even up to reduction) when G^{der} is not simply connected"; the correct condition bounds the connected component of the affine Grassmannian at each x_i(s) rather than that of Bun_G. Any formalization must take the definition from here, not from [Var04].

items.name: Definitions 1.6, 1.12, 1.13 and Construction 1.8: the Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannian and the local model
items.statement: Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I is the ind-scheme over X^I classifying the same data as Hecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I together with a trivialization θ of G_k; for I a singleton its fibre at x is the usual affine Grassmannian G(F_x)/G(O_x). By [BD99, rem. 2.3.7 and thm. 2.12.1], which generalizes the Beauville–Laszlo descent lemma [BL95], a point may equivalently be given by G-torsors on the formal neighbourhood Γ_{Σ∞x_i} of the union of the graphs with isomorphisms over the punctured neighbourhood in the sense of Notation 1.7 (a compatible system of maps V_G → V_{G′}(NΣ_{i∈J}x_i)) and a trivialization of G_k — this works for G-torsors because a torsor is a tensor functor from representations to vector bundles. Remarque 1.9 is the factorization property: over the locus where the legs indexed by different fibres of ζ : I → J are distinct, Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I is the product of the partial ones. The Weil restrictions G_{Σn_ix_i} and G_{Σ∞x_i} act by changing θ, and for n_i large in terms of the ω_i the action on the bounded stratum factors through G_{Σn_ix_i} (Proposition 1.10, Remarque 1.11). Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱} is the reduced closed subscheme obtained as the Zariski closure of the product of the usual closed strata Gr_{x_i,ω_i} over the complement of the diagonals (Definition 1.12), and Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W} the union of those with W_{ω̱} ≠ 0 in the isotypic decomposition of W. Finally β^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱,ṉ} : Hecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱} ≅ (Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱} ×_{X^I} Bun_{G,Σn_ix_i})/G_{Σn_ix_i} (Definition 1.13), whose first component δ is smooth because Bun_{G,Σn_ix_i} is smooth over X^I (Lemme 1.14); Lemme 1.15: the forgetful morphism Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱} → Gr^{(I′_1,…)}_{I,ω̱} is projective, surjective and small; Lemme 1.16: the morphisms κ, κ̃ to the product of the partial quotients are smooth.

The smallness of Lemme 1.15 is what makes the cohomology independent of the partition.

items.name: Theorem 1.17 (= Theorem 0.9): one direction of the geometric Satake equivalence, as a functor over X^I
items.statement: For A = E or O_E there is a canonical functor W ↦ S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,A} from finite-type A-linear representations of (Ĝ)^I to G_{Σ∞x_i}-equivariant A-perverse sheaves on Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I, supported on Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W} (for A = O_E on a sufficiently large finite-type closed subscheme depending on W in an unspecified way), hence a perverse sheaf up to shift on Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W}/G_{Σn_ix_i} with the shift fixed by the condition that the pullback be perverse relative to X^I, and universally locally acyclic over X^I, with: a) for A = E and W = ⊠_iV_{ω_i} irreducible, S is the intersection sheaf of Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱}; b) (π^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{(I′_1,…)})_!S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,A} ≅ S^{(I′_1,…)}_{I,W,A}; c) for W = ⊠_jW_j, S ≅ κ̃^*(⊠_j S^{(I_j)}_{I_j,W_j,A}) (compatibility with convolution); d) for ζ : I → J, Δ_ζ^*(S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,A}) ≅ S^{(J_1,…,J_k)}_{J,W^ζ,A}, functorially in W and compatibly with composition of ζ (compatibility with fusion, Remarque 1.18 — this is what makes geometric Satake a tensor functor). The proof follows [Gai07, thm. 2.6] and its appendix B: Mirković–Vilonen attach a perverse sheaf to each representation of Ĝ, convolution and fusion give the ⊠-case, and the general case is S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,A} = (S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,⊠_iR,A} ⊗ W)^{Ĝ^I} with R = O(Ĝ) as an ind-object of Rep(Ĝ). Remarque 1.19: the commutativity constraint is the modified one of [MV07] (before prop. 6.3), which adds a sign when permuting two sheaves supported on odd components — by [MV07, lemme 3.9] total cohomology then sits in even degrees, so the fibre functor is tensor into vector spaces rather than super vector spaces. Remarque 1.20: Z_{Σ∞x_i} acts trivially, so S is canonically G^{ad}_{Σ∞x_i}-equivariant.
items.locator: Théorème 1.17 with Remarques 1.18–1.20, pp. 48–51; stated as Théorème 0.9 and Remarque 0.10, pp. 11–12, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.1 plans "the classical equal-characteristic geometric Satake equivalence with its pinning and commutativity normalization … Use rational ell-adic intersection complexes and specify half-Tate-twist choices", and its acceptance test is exactly the two-leg fusion of d). Note the lettering differs between Théorème 0.9 (forgetful, convolution, fusion, IC) and Théorème 1.17 (IC, forgetful, convolution, fusion). Only this direction is used, and only through the functor — the fibre functor is never used as such (p. 11).

items.name: The classical–geometric Satake comparison and the sign (−1)^{⟨2ρ,ω⟩}
items.statement: For v ∈ |X| and V irreducible with highest weight ω, h_{V,v} ∈ C_c(G(O_v)\G(F_v)/G(O_v), O_E) is the spherical function attached to χ_V by the classical Satake isomorphism, and (−1)^{⟨2ρ,ω⟩}h_{V,v} is the trace of Frob_{Gr_v/k(v)} on S^{({0})}_{{0},V,E}|_{Gr_v}, the intersection sheaf of the closed stratum Gr_{v,ω}; the h_{V,v} form a basis of the spherical Hecke algebra over O_E, and even over Z[q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}] ([Gro98, prop. 3.6]). Remarque 1.21: the sign is there because dim Gr_{v,ω} = ⟨2ρ, ω⟩, so h_{V,v} would be the trace outright had the Satake sheaves been normalized to have total cohomology in even degrees — the same normalization that gives the modified commutativity constraint, and the reason why no sign appears in Proposition 6.2.
items.locator: §1.3, pp. 51–52, with Remarque 1.21, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.1 plans the Satake normalization and half-Tate-twist choices, FA.6 the unramified Satake dictionary. This sign convention is the hinge between the geometric and the classical sides and should be pinned once, in GS.1.

items.name: Theorem 12.16: the twisted variant of geometric Satake for a non-constant group scheme over the curve
items.statement: For the non-split case one needs the twisted geometric Satake equivalence of [Zhu15, Ric14]: a canonical functor W ↦ S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,E} from finite-dimensional E-linear representations of (^LG)^I to G^{ad}_{Σ∞x_i}-equivariant perverse sheaves (up to shift) on Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I, supported on Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W}, universally locally acyclic over (X ∖ N̂)^I and satisfying the same properties b), c), d) as Theorem 1.17; the representations are those of the L-group, not merely of Ĝ, and Gr_{I,W} now serves only as a support, so no reflex field is introduced. If W factors through (^LG/Ĝ)^I = Gal(F̃/F)^I then S is supported on the section where all φ_j are isomorphisms and comes from the smooth sheaf attached to W, with fibre W at Δ(η̄). Remarque 12.17: E may be replaced by O_E, at the cost of losing the explicit description; Remarque 12.18: since the legs vary in X ∖ N̂, the shtuka stack depends only on G over X ∖ N̂ and on the compact open subgroup at N̂. A further generalization (12.9)–(12.10) fixes some legs at places v and then requires W to be a representation only of the local L-groups ^LG_{α(i)}; the trace of Frobenius on the one-leg sheaf at v is (−1)^{⟨2ρ,ω⟩}h_{V,v}.
items.locator: Théorème 12.16 with Remarques 12.17–12.18 and (12.9)–(12.10), pp. 156–159, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.1 plans "descend nonsplit data via the L-group"; the twisted Satake sources ([Zhu15], [Ric14]) are not otherwise named in the atlas and are recorded as prerequisites here. The partially-fixed-legs variant is what makes the operators S_{V,v} available in the non-split case.

items.name: Definition 2.1 (= Definitions 0.2 and 0.6): the stacks of G-shtukas with several legs and level structure
items.statement: Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} (resp. …_{N,I,ω̱}, resp. the open …^{≤μ}_{N,I,ω̱}) is the ind-stack (resp. stack) over (X ∖ N)^I classifying the data of Hecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} (resp. with the bound, resp. with G_0 ∈ Bun^{≤μ}_G) together with an isomorphism σ : ^τG_0 ≅ G_k respecting level structures; equivalently it is the fibre product of the Hecke correspondence with the graph of the Frobenius of Bun_{G,N} (Remarque 0.3). A point is written ((x_i)_{i∈I}, (G_0, ψ_0) → ⋯ → (^τG_0, ^τψ_0)). G(O_N) acts by changing the level structure. For G = GL_r, I = {1,2}, ω_1 = (1,0,…,0), ω_2 = (0,…,0,−1) the two orders of the partition give Drinfeld’s left and right shtukas [Dri87], with x_1 and x_2 the zero and the pole; the truncations differ from those of [Laf02a] but the inductive systems are comparable. The x_i are the legs and 𝔭^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} : Cht → (X ∖ N)^I the characteristic morphism (Notation 2.3). An I-tuple ω̱ is admissible if [Σ_iω_i] = 0 in π_1(G) (Definition 2.4), equivalently, dually, if Z_Ĝ acts trivially on ⊗_iV_{ω_i} (Remarque 2.5).
