items.note: GS.2 plans "a multi-leg global shtuka as successive modifications together with an isomorphism to the pullback by Frobenius … Construct bounds, level, partial Frobenius and HN truncations", naming this paper as its source. Unlike [Var04] the stack is required to be reduced (which does not affect étale cohomology).

items.name: Proposition 2.6 and Remark 2.19: the basic geometry of the shtuka stacks
items.statement: Proposition 2.6 (a variant of [Var04, prop. 2.16]): a) Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱} is a Deligne–Mumford stack over (X ∖ N)^I, locally of finite type, and the connected components of the ≤μ-truncation are quotients of quasi-projective schemes by finite groups, and are quasi-projective schemes as soon as dim O_N is large in terms of μ and ω̱; b) it is a finite étale Galois covering of the level-free stack with group G(O_N); c) legs with ω_i = 0 split off as factors (X ∖ N)^{I∖J}; d) if all ω_i = 0 the stack is (X ∖ N)^I times the discrete stack Bun_{G,N}(F_q); e) it is non-empty if and only if ω̱ is admissible. Remarque 2.19: the open Cht^0_{N,I,ω̱} where the legs are pairwise distinct and the relative positions are exactly ω_i is smooth and dense, non-empty exactly for ω̱ admissible, the forgetful morphism is an isomorphism above it, and its preimage is dense — all of this after quotienting by Ξ as well.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6 and Remarque 2.19, pp. 53–54 and 60–61 ([Var04, prop. 2.16, cor. 2.21]; generalizing [Dri87, props. 2.3 and 3.2]), arXiv v10
items.note: GS.2 plans "the needed representability/Deligne–Mumford and finite-type statements with their stabilizer hypotheses" and its acceptance test "a rank-one shtuka over a finite field checks the Frobenius condition"; d) is the statement that makes the no-leg case the space of automorphic functions.

items.name: Propositions 2.8 and 2.9: the shtuka stacks are smooth over the affine-Grassmannian local model
items.statement: Proposition 2.8 (new here, not in [Var04]): ϵ^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{(I),ω̱,ṉ} : Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱} → Gr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,ω̱}/G_{Σn_ix_i} is smooth of dimension dim G_{Σn_ix_i} = (Σ_in_i)dim G. The proof realizes the fibre product over a point z of the Grassmannian as the equalizer of the level-forgetting morphism b_1 : Bun_{G,Σn_ix_i} ×_{X^I} S → Bun_G × S, which is smooth of that dimension, and of b_2 = (Frob_{Bun_G} × Id) ∘ (a_z, Id) where a_z is "modification by z"; b_2 has zero derivative in the fibres because the Frobenius of Bun_G does, so the equalizer is smooth. Proposition 2.9 (also new): the broken-up variant ϵ^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{(I_1,…,I_k),ω̱,ṉ} to ∏_j Gr^{(I_j)}_{I_j,(ω_i)_{i∈I_j}}/G_{Σ_{i∈I_j}n_ix_i} is smooth, being κ̃ ∘ ϵ_{(I)} with κ̃ smooth by Lemme 1.16. Remarque 2.10 gives the common generalization for a refinement (J_{j,l})_{j,l} of the partition, and notes that consequently, locally for the smooth topology, the stacks of G-shtukas are isomorphic to closed strata of Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannians or products of them — but the local model is not smooth unless all I_j are singletons and all coweights minuscule. The morphism does not factor through the quotient by Ξ (as an anonymous referee pointed out), but its composite with Gr/G_{Σn_ix_i} → Gr/G^{ad}_{Σn_ix_i} does, giving (2.10) and its level version, smooth of dimension (Σn_i)dim G^{ad}.
items.locator: Propositions 2.8–2.9 with Remarque 2.10 and (2.10), pp. 54–60; stated at (0.12) and p. 8, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.2 plans "smooth local-model maps to bounded Grassmannians". These two propositions and Proposition 2.11 are the only parts of §2 not taken from [Var04]; the Ξ-descent through G^{ad} is the correction the referee forced and is easy to get wrong.

items.name: Proposition 2.11 and Lemma 2.13: the étale-local structure of the shtuka stacks
items.statement: Proposition 2.11 (a constructive variant of [Var04, thm. 2.20]): locally for the étale topology, Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱} is isomorphic to ∏_{j=1}^k Gr^{(I_j)}_{I_j,(ω_i)_{i∈I_j}}, compatibly with the morphism ϵ of Proposition 2.9; precisely, given étale charts α_j × (x_i)_{i∈I_j} : U_j → Bun_{G,N} × (X ∖ N)^{I_j} carrying a trivialization of the universal torsor on Γ_{Σ_{i∈I_j}n_ix_i}, the induced β : U → ∏_j Gr^{(I_j)}_{I_j,(ω_i)} is étale. Lemma 2.13 (a small generalization of [Var04, lemme 4.3]) is the engine: for W, Z, T of finite type over F_q with h = (h_1, h_2) : W → Z × T étale, f : W → Z arbitrary and Z smooth, the locus U = {w : h_1(w) = Frob_Z(f(w))} has h_2 : U → T étale — proved by reducing to Z = A^m and computing the Jacobian, where the Frobenius contributes a zero block. Unlike [Var04, §4] the proof does not use the Drinfeld–Simpson theorem [DS95, thm. 2]. Remarque 2.12 gives the refinement for (J_{j,l})_{j,l}.
items.locator: Propositions 2.11, Lemme 2.13 and Remarque 2.12, pp. 56–59, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.2 plans the local models; Lemme 2.13 is the elementary reason why "intersecting with the graph of Frobenius" preserves étaleness, and is worth isolating as a lemma about schemes. The paper notes that Proposition 2.11 is not used later.

items.name: The Harder–Narasimhan truncations, the lattice Ξ and the intersection sheaf
items.statement: For a dominant coweight μ of G^{ad}, Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k),≤μ}_{N,I,ω̱} is the open where the Harder–Narasimhan polygon of the G^{ad}-torsor attached to G_0 is ≤ μ (defined by deg B_λ ≤ ⟨μ, λ⟩ for every B-structure; [Var04, lemme A.3] gives openness and finite-type components). Z(F)\Z(A) acts through Bun_{Z,N}(F_q) by twisting; the action preserves the truncations, because they are taken on the G^{ad}-torsor, and commutes with the partial Frobenius morphisms. A lattice Ξ ⊂ Z(F)\Z(A) is fixed once and for all, and Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k),≤μ}_{N,I,ω̱}/Ξ is a Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type (Lemme 12.19 in the non-split case). F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱,Ξ,E} (Definition 2.14) is its intersection sheaf, normalized relative to (X ∖ N)^I. Corollaire 2.15: F is canonically the pullback of the Satake sheaf S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,⊠V_{ω_i},E} along the smooth morphism of Proposition 2.8; Corollaire 2.16 is the broken-up version; Corollaire 2.18: the forgetful morphism Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱}/Ξ → Cht^{(I′_1,…)}_{N,I,ω̱}/Ξ is projective, surjective and small, so its Rπ_! preserves F — which is why the cohomology below does not depend on the partition.
items.locator: §2.3, Définition 2.14, Corollaires 2.15, 2.16, 2.18 and Remarque 2.17, pp. 59–60; pp. 4–5 and 12 of the introduction, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.0 plans the Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens and their finite type; GS.2 the HN truncations of the shtuka stacks; EDC.5 the intersection complex and smallness. "Nonproperness and unbounded HN degree remain visible" (GS.2) is the same caveat the paper works under.

items.name: §3: the partial Frobenius morphisms and their action on the intersection sheaves
items.statement: Fr^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I_1,N,I} : Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} → Cht^{(I_2,…,I_k,I_1)}_{N,I} sends a chain to the one obtained by dropping (G_0, ψ_0) and appending (^τG_1, ^τψ_1) through ^τφ_1, and lies over Frob_{I_1} : (X ∖ N)^I → (X ∖ N)^I, which raises the coordinates in I_1 to the q-th power; partial Frobenius morphisms are Drinfeld’s [Dri78, Dri87] and the generalization is evident. Lemme 3.1: they do not preserve the truncations but act on the inductive system, with the explicit bounds (Fr_{I_1})^{-1}(Cht^{≤μ}) ⊂ Cht^{≤μ+Σ_{i∈I_1}ω_i} and Fr_{I_1}(Cht^{≤μ}) ⊂ Cht^{≤μ−w_0(Σ_{i∈I_1}ω_i)}, w_0 the longest Weyl element. Remarque 3.2: the composite of the k partial Frobenius morphisms is the total Frobenius over F_q, so each is a totally radicial local homeomorphism. Proposition 3.3: hence a canonical isomorphism F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I_1,N,I} : (Fr_{I_1})^*(F^{(I_2,…,I_k,I_1)}_{N,I,ω̱,Ξ,E}) ≅ F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱,Ξ,E}, into which the scalar q^{−d/2} is incorporated by convention, d being the dimension of the stratum Gr^{(I_1)}_{I_1,(ω_i)_{i∈I_1}}, with signs governed by the modified commutativity constraint. Proposition 3.4: this is compatible with the Mirković–Vilonen comparison isomorphisms of Corollaire 2.16 and the canonical F_1 on the Satake side, the square being Cartesian up to totally radicial local homeomorphisms (Remarque 3.5).
items.locator: §3, Lemme 3.1, Remarques 3.2, 3.5, Propositions 3.3–3.4 and (3.5), pp. 62–64; (0.6) and pp. 8–9, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.2 plans partial Frobenius truncations and GS.4 the partial Frobenius action. The increase of μ is exactly what prevents a direct application of Drinfeld’s lemma and forces the Hecke-finite sector; the q^{−d/2} normalization is the one that makes Proposition 6.2 sign-free.

items.name: §4.1: the formalism of cohomological correspondences
items.statement: Following [SGA5], [Var07] and [BV06]: a correspondence from X_1 to X_2 is a morphism a = (a_1, a_2) : A → X_1 × X_2 of stacks locally of finite type over F_q with a_2 representable of finite type; a cohomological correspondence from F_1 to F_2 supported on A is a morphism u : a_{2,!}(a_1^*F_1) → F_2, equivalently u : a_1^*F_1 → a_2^!F_2. If a_1 is proper and p_i : X_i → Y satisfy p_1 ∘ a_1 = p_2 ∘ a_2, then u induces H(u) : p_{1,!}F_1 → p_{2,!}F_2. Correspondences compose through C = A ×_{X_2} B using proper base change ã_{2,!}b̃_2^* ≅ b_2^*a_{2,!}, and H(v ∘ u) = H(v) ∘ H(u) when the relevant legs are proper. All the operators of the paper — the partial Frobenius action F_J, the Hecke operators T(f), the creation and annihilation morphisms — are instances of this formalism, and the compatibilities between them are proved by composing correspondences.
items.note: EDC.8 plans exactly this: "cohomological correspondences c₂*K → c₁^!K, their composition when the required properness/base-change maps exist, and the trace class on the fixed-point scheme … compatibility with proper pushforward and restriction". The stacky case needed here (a_2 representable of finite type, the source only locally of finite type) should be part of that stage’s contract.

items.name: Definitions 4.1, 4.5 and 4.7: the cohomology sheaves and the functor W ↦ H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W}
items.statement: Definition 4.1: since Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k),≤μ}_{N,I,ω̱}/Ξ is a finite-type Deligne–Mumford stack, [LMB99, LO08] give H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,ω̱} = R(𝔭^{≤μ}_{N,I})_!(F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱,Ξ,E}|…) ∈ D^b_c((X ∖ N)^I, E), independent of the partition by Corollaire 2.18, with cohomology sheaves H^{i,≤μ,E}_{N,I,ω̱}; Remarque 4.2: for I = ∅ this is C_c(Bun^{≤μ}_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E) in degree 0; Remarque 4.3: for deg N′ large the truncated stack is representable quasi-projective, so étale cohomology of schemes and coinvariants under a finite group would suffice. The definition actually used is the functorial one: F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W,Ξ,E} = (ϵ^{(I_1,…,I_k),Ξ}_{N,(I),W,ṉ})^*(S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,E}) (Definition 4.5), which for irreducible W is the intersection sheaf (Remarque 4.6, canonically once V_{ω_i} is *defined* as the total cohomology of the corresponding intersection sheaf), and H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} = R(𝔭^{≤μ}_{N,I})_!(F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W,Ξ,E}|…) (Definition 4.7), an E-linear functor in W with morphisms H(u) (Notation 4.9) and isotypic decomposition H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} = ⊕_{ω̱}H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,ω̱} ⊗_E W_{ω̱} (Remarque 4.8) — the last formula displays functoriality but is much less convenient for coalescence. Proposition 4.10 gives the broken-up description of F, compatible with the partial Frobenius at I_1.
items.locator: Définitions 4.1, 4.5, 4.7, Notations 4.4, 4.9, Remarques 4.2, 4.3, 4.6, 4.8, Proposition 4.10, pp. 65–69; Définitions 0.4 and 0.11, pp. 5 and 12–13, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.3 plans "compactly supported intersection cohomology on bounded truncations and its transition maps, then the filtered colimit used for shtukas", with this paper as its source. Only the degree-zero cohomology sheaf is used later, which is why the conjectural description (0.43) sees only the diagonal G_m ⊂ SL_2 of an Arthur parameter.

items.name: Construction 2.20 and §4.4: Hecke correspondences and the operators T(f)
items.statement: Construction 2.20: for a finite set 𝔗 of places and g ∈ G(A) with g_v ∈ K_{N,v} for v ∉ 𝔗, g induces a finite étale representable self-correspondence Γ_N(g) of Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,ω̱} restricted to the legs outside |N| ∪ 𝔗, depending only on the double class K_NgK_N, presented at a deeper level N′ by the right action of g on level structures; there is κ with Γ_N(g) and its transpose carrying Cht^{≤μ} into Cht^{≤μ+κ}. When |N| ∩ 𝔗 = ∅ the class is given by coweights (λ_t)_{t∈𝔗} and Γ_N(g) classifies two shtukas linked by κ_0 : G_0|_{(X∖𝔗)×S} ≅ G′_0|_{(X∖𝔗)×S} of relative position λ_t at t. §4.4: hence for f ∈ C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, E) and κ large, morphisms T(f) : H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,ω̱}|_{(X∖𝔗)^I} → H^{≤μ+κ,E}_{N,I,ω̱}|_{(X∖𝔗)^I} with T(f_1f_2) = T(f_1)T(f_2), defined by the finite correspondences or equivalently by cohomological correspondences (and over O_E if f is), commuting with the partial Frobenius action. Proposition 4.14: the partial Frobenius action and the Hecke operators are compatible with the morphisms H(u) and with the coalescence isomorphisms, and for j ∈ J, Δ_ζ^*(F_{ζ^{-1}({j})}) corresponds to F_{{j}}.
items.locator: Construction 2.20, pp. 61–62, §§4.3–4.4 and Proposition 4.14, pp. 66–70; (0.7), pp. 5–6, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.3 plans "Hecke correspondences, cohomological correspondences and adjunction maps on that colimit with coefficient and support control"; GS.4 the commutation of the partial Frobenius with them. That these morphisms extend to all of (X ∖ N)^I is the content of Corollaire 6.5 and is not formal.

items.name: Proposition 4.12 (= Definition 0.12): the coalescence isomorphisms χ_ζ
items.statement: For ζ : I → J with diagonal Δ_ζ : X^J → X^I and W^ζ the representation of Ĝ^J obtained from W through Ĝ^J → Ĝ^I, (g_j) ↦ (g_{ζ(i)}), the canonical isomorphism d) of Theorem 1.17 gives a canonical isomorphism χ_ζ : Δ_ζ^*(H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,W}) ≅ H^{≤μ,E}_{N,J,W^ζ} in D^b_c((X ∖ N)^J, E), functorial in W and compatible with composition of ζ — the coalescence isomorphism, after [BV06, rem. 2.3.2] and [Var04]. It is enough to treat ζ injective, where it follows from Proposition 2.6 c), and ζ surjective, where the tautological isomorphism Cht^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I} ×_{(X∖N)^I}(X ∖ N)^J ≅ Cht^{(J_1,…,J_k)}_{N,J} together with d) identifies the perverse sheaves and proper base change gives the isomorphism on cohomology. Remarque 4.13: no shift or Tate twist appears, because the intersection sheaves have been normalized relative to the powers of X; and the modified commutativity constraint is used — the simplest instance being ζ a permutation of I, i.e. a change of the order of the legs. The paper reserves "coalescence" for legs fusing on the curve and "fusion" for the fusion product of perverse sheaves.
items.locator: Proposition 4.12 with Remarques 4.13–4.14, pp. 69–70; Définition 0.12 and Remarque 0.13, pp. 12–13, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.4 plans "specializing legs with explicit independence and coalescence isomorphisms"; the canonicity of Definition 4.5 is what makes this construction possible, since source and target live on different spaces.

items.name: Definitions 5.1–5.2 and Lemma 5.3 (= Definition 0.14): the creation and annihilation morphisms
items.statement: Let I, J be finite sets, ζ_J : J → {0}, ζ^I_J = (Id_I, ζ_J), W and U representations of (Ĝ)^I and (Ĝ)^J, and x ∈ U, ξ ∈ U^* invariant under the diagonal Ĝ, i.e. morphisms x : 1 → U^{ζ_J} and ξ : U^{ζ_J} → 1 of Ĝ-representations. The creation morphism C^♯_x is the composite of χ_{ζ^I_∅}, H(Id_W ⊠ x) and χ^{-1}_{ζ^I_J}, from H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} ⊠ E_{X∖N} to H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I∪J,W⊠U}|_{(X∖N)^I×Δ(X∖N)}; the annihilation morphism C^♭_ξ is the analogous composite in the other direction. By Proposition 4.14 they commute with the Hecke operators and with F_K for K ⊂ I, and they intertwine F_J with the natural partial Frobenius action on E_{X∖N}. Lemme 5.3 records the commutation and composition rules: a creation at one point and an annihilation at another commute; two creations commute and their restriction to the diagonal is C^♯_{x_1⊠x_2}; likewise for annihilations.
items.locator: Définitions 5.1–5.2, Lemme 5.3 and (5.1), pp. 70–72; Définition 0.14, pp. 13–14, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.4 plans "Verify creation/annihilation and partial Frobenius commute with Hecke operators", which is exactly Proposition 4.14 plus Lemme 5.3.

items.name: Remark 5.4: Verdier duality, the Chevalley involution and the transposition of creation and annihilation
items.statement: Let θ be a Chevalley involution of Ĝ, with θ(t) = t^{−1} on T̂. Normalizing Verdier duality relative to X^I, Theorem 1.17 gives a canonical isomorphism 𝔻(S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,E}) ≅ S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W^{*,θ},E}, functorial in W, where W^{*,θ} is the contragredient composed with θ^I; hence Cht^{≤μ}_{N,I,W} = Cht^{≤μ}_{N,I,W^{*,θ}} and 𝔻(F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W,Ξ,E}) ≅ F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W^{*,θ},Ξ,E}, canonically, functorially in W and compatibly with coalescence. This yields a pairing 𝔅^{Ξ,E}_{N,I,W} : H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W^{*,θ}} ⊗ H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} → E_{(X∖N)^I}, for which the creation and annihilation morphisms are transposes of one another. Consequences: the transpose of an excursion operator is an excursion operator (used in Remarque 12.15 to argue that B would be reduced if Conjecture 12.12 held), and Remarque 9.2 characterizes the excursion operators by this bilinear form.
items.locator: Remarque 5.4 with (5.2)–(5.3), pp. 72–73; used in Remarques 9.2 and 12.15, arXiv v10
items.note: EDC.1 owns Verdier duality; ES6:duality plans "compatibility of duality with the Chevalley/contragredient involution" in the Fargues–Scholze local setting — this is the global shtuka counterpart, and the two should share the convention. Note the duality here is normalized relative to X^I, not absolutely.

items.name: Definition 0.15 and §12.3.3: the operators S_{V,v} (create two legs, apply the partial Frobenius, annihilate)
items.statement: For v a place of X ∖ N and V an irreducible representation of Ĝ, S_{V,v} is defined, for κ large in terms of deg(v) and V, as the composite of the creation morphism C^♯_{δ_V} attached to δ_V : 1 → V ⊗ V^* (which creates two legs at v), the deg(v)-th power of the partial Frobenius F_{{1}} at the first of them, and the annihilation morphism C^♭_{ev_V}; since creation and annihilation intertwine the Frobenius action on E_v with F_{{1,2}} = F_{{1}}F_{{2}}, and F_{{1}} commutes with F_{{1,2}}, the composite descends along Z/deg(v)Z to S_{V,v} : H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} → H^{0,≤μ+κ,E}_{N,I,W} on (X ∖ N)^I. In the non-split case (§12.3.3) the same construction is carried out with the partially-fixed-legs sheaves H^{≤μ,E}_{N,I,α,W}, the two new legs being fixed at v and V a representation of the local L-group ^LG_v; the notation (F_{{1}})^{deg(v)} is then slightly abusive, since F_{{1}} itself does not exist in that setting, and S_{V,v} is again obtained by descent.
items.note: This is the germ of an excursion operator: creation, a Frobenius move on one leg, annihilation. GS.5’s excursion construction and GS.4’s creation/annihilation both plan it.

items.name: Proposition 6.2 (= Proposition 0.16) and Corollary 6.5: S_{V,v} is the Hecke operator T(h_{V,v}), extended to all legs
items.statement: The restriction of S_{V,v} to (X ∖ (N ∪ v))^I equals, as a morphism of sheaves there, the Hecke operator T(h_{V,v}). Consequently (Corollaire 6.5) for every f ∈ C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, E) the morphism T(f) extends naturally, for κ large enough, to a morphism of constructible sheaves on the whole of (X ∖ N)^I, compatibly with composition: it suffices to treat f = h_{V,v} at one place, where the extension is S_{V,v}. The proof is geometric: two closed substacks Y_1, Y_2 of Cht^{({1},{2},I)}_{N,I∪{1,2},W⊠V⊠V^*}|_{(X∖(N∪v))^I×Δ(v)} realize the creation-then-partial-Frobenius and the annihilation as cohomological correspondences, their fibre product is canonically the finite étale Hecke correspondence Γ^{(I)}, and for V minuscule and deg(v) = 1 the two are smooth and transverse on the smooth loci, with the correction factor q^{−d/2} already built into the partial Frobenius; Remarque 6.9 shows that no sign is needed, and Remarque 6.17 that Bott–Samelson resolutions would give an alternative to the general singular case. For GL_r it is enough to treat V = Λ^kSt (Remarque 16.1).
items.locator: Proposition 6.2 and Corollaire 6.5, p. 75, with Remarques 6.9 and 6.17, pp. 78 and 101; sketched as Proposition 0.16, pp. 15–19; the non-split case is (12.16), p. 162, arXiv v10
items.note: For Shimura varieties over number fields such extensions of Hecke operators were constructed by Zariski closure or nearby cycles ([Del71, FC90, GT05], p. 19); this is the shtuka analogue, and it is what makes the Eichler–Shimura relation available at every leg.

items.name: Proposition 7.1 (= Proposition 0.17): the Eichler–Shimura relations
items.statement: Let I, W be as above, V an irreducible representation of Ĝ and v a place of X ∖ N. Then, for κ large enough in terms of deg(v) and V, Σ_{i=0}^{dim V}(−1)^i (F^{deg(v)}_{{0}})^i ∘ S_{Λ^{dim V − i}V, v}|_{(X∖N)^I×v} = 0, as morphisms lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I∪{0},W⊠V}|_{(X∖N)^I×v} → lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I∪{0},W⊠V}|_{(X∖N)^I×v}: the partial Frobenius at the leg 0 is annihilated by a polynomial of degree dim V whose coefficients are the restrictions of the morphisms S_{Λ^iV,v}, with coefficients in O_E. The proof is a tensor-algebra computation inspired by a proof of the Cayley–Hamilton theorem and using only Λ^{dim V+1}V = 0, applied to the definition of the S_{Λ^iV,v} by creation, partial Frobenius and annihilation; taking the restriction to (X ∖ N)^I × v requires the extension of the Hecke operators of Corollaire 6.5.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1, p. 102 (§7); stated as Proposition 0.17, pp. 19–20, arXiv v10
items.note: Routed as a source of GS.3 and GS.4: no stage of the atlas states an Eichler–Shimura relation for shtukas, yet GS.3's Hecke-finite finiteness and GS.4's application of Drinfeld's lemma both consume it.

items.name: Lemma 0.18 (Drinfeld): lisse sheaves on U^I with partial Frobenius actions are representations of π_1(U, η)^I
items.statement: Let E be a constructible lisse O_E-sheaf on a dense open of (X ∖ N)^I equipped with an action of the partial Frobenius morphisms, i.e. isomorphisms F_{{i}} : Frob_{{i}}^*(E)|_{η^I} → E|_{η^I} commuting with one another and with composition the natural isomorphism Frob^*(E) ≅ E. Then E extends to a lisse sheaf on U^I for U a small enough dense open of X ∖ N, the fibre E|_{∆(η)} carries an action of π_1(U, η)^I, and for fixed U the functor E ↦ E|_{∆(η)} is an equivalence from constructible lisse O_E-sheaves on U^I with partial Frobenius action to continuous representations of π_1(U, η)^I on finite-type O_E-modules, compatibly with coalescence. Moreover sp^* : E|_{∆(η)} → E|_{η^I} is then an isomorphism (Remarque 0.19).
items.locator: Lemme 0.18 and Remarque 0.19, p. 21 (Drinfeld, [Dri78, Thm. 2.1] and [Dri89, Prop. 6.1]; see also [Lau04]); §8, pp. 106–127, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.4 plans "Drinfeld's lemma in the exact lisse/finite-rank setting first, then justify its use on the Hecke-finite sector" — the two-step structure of this paper.

items.name: Remark 0.24 and §8: the group FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) and the factorization of its action
items.statement: FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) := {ε ∈ Aut_{F_q}(F̄_I) : ∃(n_i)_{i∈I} ∈ Z^I, ε|_{(F_I)^{perf}} = ∏_{i∈I}(Frob_{{i}})^{n_i}} is an extension of Z^I by Ker(π_1(η^I, η̄^I) → Ẑ), and for I a singleton it is the usual Weil group π_1(η, η̄) ×_Ẑ Z. A choice of specialization arrow sp gives an inclusion F̄ ⊗_{F_q} ⋯ ⊗_{F_q} F̄ ⊂ F̄_I and hence a surjection FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) → Weil(η, η̄)^I; the statement that the Hecke-finite part carries an action of π_1(η, η̄)^I is equivalent to saying that the natural FWeil-action factors through this surjection, and even through π_1(η, η̄)^I.
items.locator: Remarque 0.24 with (0.35), pp. 23–24; Proposition 8.27 and Remarque 8.28, pp. 119–120, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.4 plans "Construct the continuous action of a product of global Galois groups … A geometric fundamental group of C^I cannot simply be replaced by the product without the partial-Frobenius/descent theorem", which is this group and this factorization.

items.name: Definition 0.20 and Proposition 8.27 (= Lemma 0.22): the Hecke-finite part
items.statement: For a geometric point x of (X ∖ N)^I, an element of lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_x is Hecke-finite if it lies in a finite-type O_E-submodule stable under T(f) for every f ∈ C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, O_E); the Hecke-finite elements form an E-subspace stable under π_1(x, x̄) and under the Hecke algebra. Proposition 8.27: (lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_{η^I})^{Hf} is the union of the O_E-modules G|_{η^I} for G a constructible O_E-subsheaf of lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_{η^I} stable under the partial Frobenius morphisms — proved by taking, for a finite-type submodule M̌ stable under π_1 and the Hecke algebra, the sum of the F^{n_i}_{{i}}-translates of M̌ for n_i < deg(v_i) dim W_i, which is constructible and stable by the Eichler–Shimura relation. Hence FWeil, and then π_1(η, η̄)^I, acts on it (Proposition 0.23).
items.locator: Définition 0.20 and Remarque 0.21, pp. 21–22; Proposition 8.27, p. 119, with Lemmes 8.30, 8.33; stated as Lemme 0.22 and Proposition 0.23, pp. 22–23, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.3 plans "the Hecke-finite/cuspidal sector used by V. Lafforgue and prove its required finiteness; do not declare the full untruncated shtuka cohomology finite dimensional" — exactly the paper's discipline, since lim_µ H is not constructible (its fibres are infinite dimensional).

items.name: Corollary 8.34 (= Proposition 0.25): the specialization map is an isomorphism on Hecke-finite parts
items.statement: The specialization homomorphism sp^* : lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_{∆(η̄)} → lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_{η̄^I}, for a fixed geometric generic point η̄^I of X^I and a specialization arrow sp : η̄^I → ∆(η̄), restricts to an isomorphism on the Hecke-finite parts. Propositions 8.31 and 8.32 are the two halves (the image of sp^* contains, respectively is contained in, the relevant subspaces).
items.locator: Corollaire 8.34, p. 127, with Propositions 8.31–8.32, pp. 123–124; stated as Proposition 0.25, p. 24, arXiv v10
items.note: This makes Definition 0.26 independent of the choice of η̄^I and sp, which is what GS.5's "independence from auxiliary leg choices" requires.

items.name: Definition 0.26 and Proposition 9.7 (= Proposition 0.28): the spaces H_{I,W} and their three properties
items.statement: H_{I,W} := (lim_µ H^{0,≤µ,E}_{N,I,W}|_{∆(η̄)})^{Hf}, with its action of Gal(F̄/F)^I = π_1(η, η̄)^I, which is independent of the choice of η̄^I and sp (Lemme 9.4). Proposition 9.7: a) W ↦ H_{I,W}, u ↦ H(u) is an E-linear functor from finite-dimensional representations of (Ĝ)^I to inductive limits of finite-dimensional continuous E-representations of Gal(F̄/F)^I; b) for every ζ : I → J there is an isomorphism χ_ζ : H_{I,W} ≅ H_{J,W_ζ}, functorial in W, equivariant for Gal(F̄/F)^J acting through the diagonal, and compatible with composition; c) for I = ∅ and W = 1, H_{∅,1} = C^{cusp}_c(G(F)\G(A)/K_NΞ, E). All of this is compatible with the C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, E)-module structure. Remarque 0.27: this paper proves only that H_{I,W} is an inductive limit of finite-dimensional continuous representations; Cong Xue [Xue17] later proved it is finite dimensional, for split groups, and that result is not used here.
items.locator: Définition 0.26, p. 24; Proposition 9.7, p. 132, with Lemme 9.4, p. 130; stated as Proposition 0.28 and Remarque 0.27, pp. 24–26, arXiv v10
items.note: Properties a), b), c) are the whole input to the construction of the excursion operators: everything after §9 is formal consequence of them.

items.name: Proposition 8.23: cuspidal = Hecke-finite in degree zero with no legs
items.statement: The space of cuspidal functions C^{cusp}_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E) is exactly the Hecke-finite part of C_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E). Cuspidal functions are Hecke-finite because the O_E-lattice of cuspidal functions is of finite type and Hecke-stable. Conversely, if a Hecke-finite f had a non-zero constant term f_P along a proper parabolic P with Levi M, then, since the representation ring of M̂ is a finite module over that of Ĝ, f_P would be Hecke-finite for M at a place v; the Hecke operators for M at v include translations by Z_M(F_v), the support of f_P lies in a translate of a cone in the finite-type free Z-module of degrees relative to M/Z (Remarque 8.26), and that contradicts membership of a finite-dimensional Z_M(F_v)-stable space (Lemmes 8.24, 8.25).
items.locator: Proposition 8.23 with Notation 8.22, Lemmes 8.24–8.25 and Remarque 8.26, pp. 117–119; sketched on pp. 25–26, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.3's acceptance test is "At the trivial representation and no legs identify the cusp-form space exactly", which is this proposition; FA.6 owns cuspidal subspaces and their reduction-theoretic finiteness.

items.name: Definition 0.29 (= §9): the excursion operators
items.statement: For a finite set I, a finite-dimensional representation W of (Ĝ)^I, ζ_I : I → {0}, morphisms of Ĝ-representations x : 1 → W_{ζ_I} and ξ : W_{ζ_I} → 1 (that is, x ∈ W and ξ ∈ W^* invariant under the diagonal Ĝ), and (γ_i)_{i∈I} ∈ Gal(F̄/F)^I, the excursion operator S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)_{i∈I}} ∈ End(H_{{0},1}) is the composition H_{{0},1} → H_{{0},W_{ζ_I}} ≅ H_{I,W} --(γ_i)--> H_{I,W} ≅ H_{{0},W_{ζ_I}} → H_{{0},1} of H(x), χ_{ζ_I}^{-1}, the Galois action, χ_{ζ_I} and H(ξ): a creation operator which creates legs at one and the same generic point of the curve, a Galois action which moves the legs around the curve independently and brings them back, and an annihilation operator. These operators are endomorphisms of H_{{0},1} = C^{cusp}_c(G(F)\G(A)/K_NΞ, E) as a module over the Hecke algebra.
items.locator: Définition 0.29 with (0.42), pp. 26–27; §9, pp. 127–133, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "excursion operators indexed by invariant functions and Galois tuples" for the global function-field case; ES0 plans the same formal construction ("a finite leg set, a matrix coefficient/invariant function, creation by a coevaluation map, the prescribed tuple of Weil elements and annihilation by evaluation") for the Fargues–Scholze local setting. Keep the two distinct: this paper is the global source.

items.name: Lemma 10.1 (= Lemma 0.31) and Proposition 10.8 (= Proposition 0.36): the relations satisfied by the excursion operators
items.statement: Lemma 10.1: S_{I,W,x,^tu(ξ′),(γ_i)} = S_{I,W′,u(x),ξ′,(γ_i)} for a (Ĝ)^I-equivariant u : W → W′; S_{J,W_ζ,x,ξ,(γ_j)_{j∈J}} = S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_{ζ(i)})_{i∈I}}; S over a disjoint union with exterior products is the composition of the two operators; and S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i(γ′_i)^{-1}γ″_i)} = S_{I⊔I⊔I,W⊠W^*⊠W,δ_W⊠x,ξ⊠ev_W,(γ_i)×(γ′_i)×(γ″_i)}. By Observation 0.32 the functions (g_i)_{i∈I} ↦ ⟨ξ, (g_i)_{i∈I}·x⟩ obtained by varying W, x, ξ are exactly the regular functions on the coarse quotient Ĝ\(Ĝ)^I/Ĝ, and by Lemma 10.6 the operator depends only on I, that function f and (γ_i)_{i∈I}, so one may write S_{I,f,(γ_i)}. Proposition 10.8 then reformulates the relations: (i) f ↦ S_{I,f,(γ_i)} is a morphism of commutative algebras O(Ĝ\(Ĝ)^I/Ĝ) → B; (ii) S_{J,f_ζ,(γ_j)} = S_{I,f,(γ_{ζ(i)})}; (iii) S_{I⊔I⊔I,f̃,(γ_i)×(γ′_i)×(γ″_i)} = S_{I,f,(γ_i(γ′_i)^{-1}γ″_i)} for f̃((g_i)×(g′_i)×(g″_i)) = f((g_i(g′_i)^{-1}g″_i)); (iv) (γ_i)_{i∈I} ↦ S_{I,f,(γ_i)} is continuous for the E-adic topology on B. Remarque 10.9: S_{I,f,(γ_i)} = S_{I,f,(γ_iγ)} for any γ.
items.locator: Lemme 10.1, p. 133, Lemme 10.6 and Notation 10.7, p. 138, Proposition 10.8, p. 138, Remarque 10.9, p. 139; stated as Lemmes 0.31, 0.33, Observation 0.32, Définition 0.34 and Proposition 0.36, pp. 28–30, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "prove the relations and commutativity"; ES0 plans "linearity, multiplication, reindexing, unit insertion and composition relations … continuity in Weil variables"; LP2:excursion-presentation owns the algebra of invariant functions on tuples. The proofs here use only properties a) and b) of Proposition 9.7.

items.name: Notation 10.5 and the spectral decomposition (0.51): the excursion algebra B
items.statement: B ⊂ End_{C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N,E)}(C^{cusp}_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E)) is the E-subalgebra generated by all excursion operators; it is commutative by the disjoint-union relation. It is not known whether B is reduced (Remarque 11.6), but a spectral decomposition — a decomposition into generalized eigenspaces, not a simultaneous diagonalization — gives H_{{0},1} = ⊕_ν H_ν over the characters ν of B, after enlarging E so that all characters of B are defined over E. Remarque 11.6 records that the subalgebra B_1 generated by the Θ_1(f) is generated by the Hecke operators at the places of X ∖ N.
items.locator: Notation 10.5, p. 137, Remarque 11.6, p. 142, and (0.51), p. 30, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "Record nilpotents/generalized eigenspaces rather than assuming simultaneous diagonalizability" — the same warning the paper gives (p. 30: "we do not know how to show that they are diagonalizable").

items.name: Lemmas 10.2 and 10.4 (= Lemma 0.39): Hecke operators at unramified places are excursion operators
items.statement: Let v be a place of X ∖ N, with a fixed embedding F̄ ⊂ F̄_v, and γ ∈ Gal(F̄_v/F_v) ⊂ Gal(F̄/F) with deg(γ) = d. Then S_{{1,2},V⊠V^*,δ_V,ev_V,(γ,1)} depends only on d, and for d = 1 it equals T(h_{V,v}). The proof is the commutativity of a diagram in which the left-hand column is creation at v, the deg(v)d-th power of the partial Frobenius and annihilation — that is, S_{V,v} for d = 1 — and the right-hand column is the excursion operator, the two being linked by the specialization isomorphisms sp_v^*; Proposition 6.2 then identifies the left column with T(h_{V,v}). Remarque 10.3 notes that a formal tensor computation determines these operators for arbitrary d, and Remarque 0.40 that other d bring nothing new.
items.locator: Lemmes 10.2 and 10.4, pp. 135–136, with Remarque 10.3; stated as Lemme 0.39 and Remarque 0.40, pp. 35–36, arXiv v10
items.note: This is the bridge between the excursion algebra and the classical Hecke algebra, and hence the source of the Satake compatibility in Theorem 11.11.

items.name: Proposition 11.7 (= Proposition 0.37): a compatible system of invariant evaluations comes from a unique semisimple parameter
items.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group and H a reductive group over E, not necessarily connected, with H^0 split. Suppose given, for every n ∈ N^*, an algebra morphism Ξ_n : O((H)^n//H^0) → C(Γ^n, E) — regular functions on H^n invariant under diagonal conjugation by H^0 — such that a) the sequence is functorial for all maps between the sets {1, …, n}, Ξ_n(f^ζ)((γ_j)) = Ξ_m(f)((γ_{ζ(i)})) for f^ζ((g_j)) = f((g_{ζ(i)})), and b) Ξ_{n+1}(f̂)(γ_1, …, γ_{n+1}) = Ξ_n(f)(γ_1, …, γ_nγ_{n+1}) for f̂(g_1, …, g_{n+1}) = f(g_1, …, g_ng_{n+1}). Then there is a continuous morphism σ : Γ → H(E′), E′/E finite, whose image has reductive Zariski closure in H_{E′}, with f(σ(γ_1), …, σ(γ_n)) = (Ξ_n(f))(γ_1, …, γ_n) for all n, f and (γ_i); and the σ with these properties form a single H^0(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugacy class. H is allowed to be disconnected because §12 applies the proposition with H = ^LG_E and H^0 = Ĝ_E; for a split G it is applied with H = H^0 = Ĝ_E and Γ = π_1(X ∖ N, η̄), to the system Θ^ν_n = ν ∘ Θ_n attached to a character ν of B, and yields the Langlands parameter σ with (C1) values in Ĝ(E′) and continuity, (C2) reductive Zariski closure of the image, (C3) ν(S_{I,f,(γ_i)}) = f((σ(γ_i))_{i∈I}) and (C4) factorization through π_1(X ∖ N, η̄); ν and the conjugacy class of σ then determine each other.
items.locator: Proposition 11.7, p. 143, with the proof and Lemmes 11.9–11.10, pp. 144–147, and (C1)–(C4), pp. 147–148; stated as Proposition 0.37, pp. 30–34, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.5 plans "reconstruct continuous semisimple L-group parameters from characters of the excursion algebra". LP2:semisimple-characters plans the Fargues–Scholze local analogue (FS VIII.3.8) for the Weil group of a local field with finite wild ramification; this is the global profinite statement, for a possibly disconnected H with H^0 split, and the two should cite one another rather than be proved twice. The invariant-theoretic input is routed separately below.

items.name: Notation 11.1, Lemma 11.9 (Richardson) and the invariant theory the reconstruction rests on
items.statement: Notation 11.1: O((H_E)^n//H^0_E) is the algebra of regular functions on H^n invariant under diagonal conjugation, of finite type by Hilbert [Hil1893] (see [MFK94, I.2]), so that (H_E)^n//H^0_E = Spec of it is the coarse quotient. Following [Ric88], an n-tuple (g_1, …, g_n) ∈ H(Q̄_ℓ)^n is semisimple if the Zariski closure ⟨g_1, …, g_n⟩ of the group it generates is reductive; in characteristic zero this is equivalent to every parabolic containing the tuple containing an associated Levi containing it [Ser05]. Lemma 11.9 (Richardson): the tuple is semisimple if and only if its H^0_{Q̄_ℓ}-conjugacy class is closed in (H_{Q̄_ℓ})^n; and the closed H^0-orbits correspond to the Q̄_ℓ-points of the coarse quotient. This is [Ric88, Thm. 3.6] with the quotient taken by H^0 rather than H — the proof adapts because the contradiction in one direction is produced by a cocharacter, which lands in H^0, and the other direction applies the Hilbert–Mumford theorem [Ric88, Thm. 2.1] to the H^0-action — together with the general properties of coarse quotients [Ric88, 1.3.2]. The reconstruction also uses [Ric88, Thm. 5.2]: if (h_1, …, h_n) lies over the same point of the coarse quotient as a semisimple (g_1, …, g_n), then ⟨g_1, …, g_n⟩ is conjugate to a Levi subgroup of ⟨h_1, …, h_n⟩. Remarque 11.2 cites [Pro76, Ric88, Vin96] for these characteristic-zero quotients and [LM85, CW82] for the older moduli-of-representations literature, and §0.9 traces the idea to Poincaré [Poi1884].
items.locator: Notation 11.1 and Remarque 11.2, pp. 140–141, Lemme 11.9, p. 144, and the uses of [Ric88, Thm. 5.2] in Lemme 11.10, p. 145; §0.9, pp. 37–38, arXiv v10
items.note: Routed as a source of LanglandsParameterStacks LP2 and LP3: the characteristic-zero invariant theory of H^n under diagonal H^0-conjugation that the whole reconstruction rests on, and which the atlas's integral Fargues–Scholze stages consume without stating.

items.name: Remark 11.8: the GL_r case through pseudo-characters
items.statement: For H = GL_r Proposition 11.7 is classical: the sequence (Θ_n) is determined by Θ_1(Tr), which must be the character of σ, and Λ^{r+1}St = 0 gives the pseudo-character relation, whence the existence of σ by Taylor [Tay91]. This is why the paper obtains nothing new for G = GL_r, where everything was already known from Drinfeld (r = 2) and Laurent Lafforgue.
items.locator: Remarque 11.8, p. 143, with p. 32 of the introduction, arXiv v10
items.note: Routed with the previous item: pseudo-characters and their Taylor reconstruction are the GL_r shadow of the general invariant-theoretic argument, and no stage of the atlas plans them (the string "pseudo-character" does not occur in the atlas).

items.name: Lemma 11.10 and the proof of Proposition 11.7: the maximality choices, the homomorphism property and continuity
items.statement: For (n, (γ_1, …, γ_n)) one writes ξ_n(γ_1, …, γ_n) for the point of (H)^n//H^0 attached to the character f ↦ Ξ_n(f)(γ_1, …, γ_n) and ξ^{ss}_n for the corresponding class of semisimple tuples, C(g_1, …, g_n) for its centralizer in H^0 and D(g_1, …, g_n) for the centralizer of C — both reductive, the centralizer of a reductive subgroup in a reductive group being reductive. One selects (n, (γ_i)) with dim⟨g_1, …, g_n⟩ maximal, then dim C minimal, then the number of connected components of C minimal. Lemma 11.10: for every γ ∈ Γ there is a unique g with (g_1, …, g_n, g) ∈ ξ^{ss}_{n+1}(γ_1, …, γ_n, γ), and then C(g_1, …, g_n, g) = C(g_1, …, g_n) and g ∈ D(g_1, …, g_n); existence uses condition a) and [Ric88, Thm. 5.2] with the maximality of the dimension, uniqueness the minimality of C. Setting σ(γ) = g gives a homomorphism, because (g_1, …, g_n, g, g′) and (g_1, …, g_n, gg′) are semisimple and conditions a), b) place them over the right points. σ takes values in H(E′) because g is determined by the image of (g_1, …, g_n, g) in (H)^{n+1}//H^0, which is defined over E. Continuity follows from the surjectivity of O((H_{E′})^{n+1}//H^0_{E′}) → O(D(g_1, …, g_n)), which factors through O(H_{E′}//C(g_1, …, g_n)) = O(H_{E′})^{C(g_1,…,g_n)}: the conjugation orbit of a semisimple tuple is a closed affine subvariety isomorphic to H^0/C, the quotient of a reductive group by a reductive subgroup being affine, and restriction to D stays surjective on C-invariants by complete reducibility of representations of the reductive C (the Reynolds operator, [MFK94, §I.1]). Finally all the tuples (σ(γ_1), …, σ(γ_n), σ(δ_1), …, σ(δ_m)) are semisimple, so the closure of the image of σ is reductive, and σ is unique up to H^0(Q̄_ℓ)-conjugacy since its construction was forced by the choice of (g_1, …, g_n).
items.locator: Lemme 11.10, p. 145, and the proof of Proposition 11.7, pp. 144–147; sketched on pp. 32–34, arXiv v10
items.note: Routed with the invariant theory: these are the steps that turn Richardson's theorems into a continuous homomorphism, and they are what LP2:semisimple-characters means by "construct the representative from the compatible invariant evaluations, prove simultaneous conjugacy/complete reducibility and continuity".

items.name: §12.1–12.3: the non-split case — L-group, ker^1(F, G), inner forms and Bruhat–Tits models
items.statement: For G connected reductive over F, not necessarily split, one fixes a smooth model over X ∖ N̂ (Bruhat–Tits), the dual group Ĝ with the finite-image Galois action and the L-group ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(F̄/F). Lemme 12.1 ([Beh91], [Hei10, ex. (1) p. 504], [AH13, Prop. 2.2, Thm. 2.5]) supplies the vector bundle needed for the geometry of Bun_G in this generality. Remarque 12.2: the inclusion G(F)\G(A)/K_N ⊂ Bun_{G,N}(F_q) has image the locally trivial G-bundles, and Bun_{G,N}(F_q) is the disjoint union, over ker^1(F, G), of the adelic quotients for the corresponding inner forms — which is why Theorem 12.3 decomposes a sum of cuspidal spaces for inner forms. Langlands parameters are then continuous semisimple sections of ^LG over Gal(F̄/F) up to Ĝ-conjugacy; Proposition 12.5 compares parameters under a morphism G′ → G, and Remarque 12.13 recovers the decomposition for SL_r from GL_r.
items.locator: §§12.1–12.3, Lemme 12.1, Remarque 12.2, Proposition 12.5, Remarque 12.13, pp. 148–159, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.0 plans "descend data for nonsplit groups and retain the ramified places" and the torsor-class description of rational points; RG2.3 owns parahoric and congruence group schemes (the Bruhat–Tits models Heinloth helped with, p. 38); RG2.5 owns the L-group.

items.name: Conjecture 12.7 (with Remarks 12.6, 12.8–12.11): the parameters should come from elliptic Arthur parameters
items.statement: Conjecture 12.7: every Langlands parameter σ occurring in the decomposition (12.5) is of the form σ_ψ for ψ an elliptic Arthur parameter. Remarque 12.8 hopes to prove it using the Lefschetz SL_2-actions on the cohomology of compactifications; Remarque 12.9 would like a decomposition of the whole discrete part, not only the cuspidal part; Remarque 12.10 notes that for groups other than GL_r multiplicities > 1 may occur in each H_σ; Remarque 12.11 records the coarser decomposition indexed by the parameters of the centre obtained through class field theory (Remarque 12.6).
items.locator: Conjecture 12.7 with Remarques 12.6 and 12.8–12.11, pp. 153–155, arXiv v10
items.note: Recorded as a conjecture and routed to GS.5 as a source: it is the expected shape of the answer, not a theorem, and GS.5's acceptance conditions explicitly exclude asserting "that every parameter occurs, packet multiplicities, or a full general-group inverse correspondence".

items.name: Conjecture 12.12 (with Remarks 12.14–12.15): the decomposition should be defined over Q and independent of ℓ
items.statement: Conjecture 12.12: the decomposition (12.5) is defined over Q and indexed by motivic Langlands parameters, and it is independent of ℓ and of the embedding Q̄ ↪ Q̄_ℓ. Remarque 12.14: granting the Tate conjecture in addition to the standard conjectures one could hope to prove it by making the constructions motivic; Remarque 12.15: it would imply the existence of an algebra B_Q with B ⊗_E Q̄_ℓ = B_Q ⊗_Q Q̄_ℓ for every embedding. Remarque 12.13 notes it is evident for GL_r.
items.locator: Conjecture 12.12 with Remarques 12.13–12.15, pp. 155–156, arXiv v10
items.note: Recorded as a conjecture and routed to GS.5 as a source, so that the stage records what is expected but unproved about the canonicity of its own output.

items.name: Proposition 13.1 and Theorem 13.2: the decomposition with F̄_ℓ coefficients
items.statement: Proposition 13.1: the O_E-lattice C^{cusp}_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, O_E) is preserved by every excursion operator S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} with W, x, ξ defined over O_E. The proof builds H^{0,≤μ,O_E}_{N,I,W} as the image of R^0(p^{≤μ}_{N,I})_!(F^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{N,I,W,Ξ,O_E}) inside the E-coefficient sheaf — "one kills the possible torsion" — shows these subsheaves are preserved by creation, annihilation, Hecke operators over O_E and the partial Frobenius morphisms, characterizes Hecke-finiteness integrally, and concludes that sp^* is an isomorphism on the integral Hecke-finite parts, so that E may be replaced by O_E throughout the definition of the excursion operators. It uses the O_E-coefficient geometric Satake of [MV07], whose argument avoids Verdier duality, so that the failure of duality to preserve the perverse t-structure integrally does not matter. Theorem 13.2: there is a canonical decomposition of C_c(K_N\G(A)/K_N, F̄_ℓ)-modules C^{cusp}_c(Bun_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, F̄_ℓ) = ⊕_σ ℌ^{F̄_ℓ}_σ indexed by the Ĝ(F̄_ℓ)-conjugacy classes of σ : π_1(X ∖ N̂, η̄) → ^LG(F̄_ℓ) that (i) take values in ^LG(F′) for a finite extension F′/F_ℓ and are continuous, (ii) have the prescribed projection to Gal(F̃/F), and (iii) are completely reducible, i.e. every parabolic of ^LG(F̄_ℓ) containing the image admits a Levi containing it; ℌ^{F̄_ℓ}_σ is the generalized eigenspace of the reduced excursion operators for the eigenvalue system ⟨ξ, (σ(γ_i))_{i∈I}·x⟩. The compatibility with Satake holds only in the generalized-eigenspace sense, and Remarque 13.3 says that containment in the honest eigenspace of h_{V,v} is presumably false in general, because the unramified Hecke operators mod ℓ need not be diagonalizable. The last paragraph of §13 relates the two decompositions: for σ : π_1(X ∖ N̂, η̄) → ^LG(Z̄_ℓ) whose rationalization satisfies the conditions of Théorème 11.11, the image of ℌ_{σ^{rat}} ∩ C^{cusp}_c(…, Z̄_ℓ) in C^{cusp}_c(…, F̄_ℓ) lies in ℌ^{F̄_ℓ}_{σ̄^{ss}}, σ̄^{ss} being the semisimplification of the reduction.
items.locator: Proposition 13.1, p. 166, Théorème 13.2, p. 168, Remarque 13.3 and the closing paragraph, p. 169 (§13), arXiv v10
items.note: Routed as a source of GS.5. No stage plans a modular-coefficient decomposition, and GS.1 defers modular Satake explicitly ("integral and modular Satake are further coefficient branches"), which Proposition 13.1 needs. Remarque 13.3 must travel with the theorem: the mod-ℓ branch is strictly weaker than GS.5's "unramified Satake compatibility".

items.name: The characteristic-ℓ complete-reducibility input of §13
items.statement: To run the reconstruction of σ over F̄_ℓ one needs complete reducibility in characteristic ℓ: Theorem 3.1 of Bate–Martin–Röhrle [BMR05], which completes in characteristic ℓ ≠ 0 the results of Richardson [Ric88] (both recapitulated as Theorem 3.7 of [Ser05]), with the details of the argument referred to the proof of Theorem 4.5 of [BHKT16]; and, for non-split G, the extension of complete reducibility to reductive groups that need not be connected (§6 of [BMR05]) together with the fact that every parabolic P of ^LG surjecting onto ^LG/Ĝ is "of Richardson type", justified through §I.3 and the proof of Lemma 3.5 of [Bor79]. One also uses that the O_E-defined functions (g_1, …, g_n) ↦ ⟨ξ, (1, g_1, …, g_n)·x⟩ are exactly the O_E-defined regular functions on (^LG)^n//Ĝ, and likewise over Z̄_ℓ and F̄_ℓ.
items.note: Routed with the characteristic-zero invariant theory to LanglandsParameterStacks LP2 and LP3: LP3 is the atlas's stage for integral reductive invariant theory and for a reductive group in characteristic ℓ, and this is exactly the input it would need. PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-THORNE (issue #1468, not yet extracted) proves the theorem referred to here.

items.name: §14: indications for metaplectic groups
items.statement: The chapter "indicates summarily" how the results extend to metaplectic groups, in a deliberately modest framework: N divides q − 1 and the metaplectic extension comes from N-th roots of even-degree line bundles with good factorization properties (the bundles A, B, B^{(I)}_I), which covers the usual metaplectic extension of Sp_{2n} but not the general K_2-extensions of [GG14, Wei14, Wei15]; for the general case one would have to use factorization gerbes over F_q in the sense of [GL16]. One forms μ_N-gerbes B̃un_G, G̃r^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I/G_{Σ∞x_i} and H̃ecke^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_I — Remarque 14.1: this is a factorization gerbe in the sense of [GL16], defined over F_q because N | q − 1 — lifts the shtuka stack to the gerbe by the trivialization A_{G_0} ⊗ A^{-1}_{^τG_0} = (A_{G_0})^{1-q} = ((A_{G_0})^{-(q-1)/N})^N, constructs an isogeny Z^♯ → Z as in [Lys15, 5.2.3] to replace the failure of the G_{Σ∞x_i}-action to factor through G^{ad}, and obtains the sheaves and the identification lim_μ H̃^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,∅,1}|_{F̄_q} = C_ζ(B̃un_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E) with B̃un_{G,N}(F_q) = ∪_{α∈ker¹(F,G)}G_α(F)\G̃_α(A)/K_N. The central input is **assumed**: that there is a group ^LG̃, an extension of Gal(F̃/F) by ^LG̃^0, for which the analogue of Théorème 12.16 holds, i.e. a canonical functor W ↦ S^{(I_1,…,I_k)}_{I,W,E} on representations of (^LG̃)^I with properties b), c), d) — its existence being justified in [FL10, Rei12, Lys14, GL16] only when G is split. Granting that, "the same arguments as in chapter 12" give a decomposition of C^{cusp}_ζ(B̃un_{G,N}(F_q)/Ξ, E) indexed by metaplectic Langlands parameters. Remarque 14.2: one may hope the F̄_ℓ-results of §13 extend, but this cannot be shown at present, because [FL10] and [Lys14] do not treat O_E coefficients.
items.note: Routed as a source of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4. The chapter proves nothing: it assumes metaplectic geometric Satake (known only in the split case) and then says the arguments of §12 apply. The route must plan it as a programme, with Lysenko's and Gaitsgory–Lysenko's papers as the sources.

items.name: §15 and Proposition 15.1: the link with the geometric Langlands programme
items.statement: For G split and N empty, the Hecke functors φ_{I,W}(F) = q_{1,!}(q_0^*(F) ⊗ F_{I,W}) on D^b_c(Bun_G, Q̄_ℓ) define what it is for F to be "proper for E": a family of isomorphisms φ_{I,W}(F) ≅ F ⊠ W_E, functorial in W and compatible with exterior products and fusion, for E a Ĝ-local system on X. The conjectures of the geometric Langlands programme imply the existence of such an F (non-zero after a Whittaker normalization). Proposition 15.1, labelled in print "conditional on a result not yet written up": if such an F is Ξ-equivariant and the function f attached to it by the sheaf-to-function dictionary, f(x) = Tr(Frob_x, F|_x), is cuspidal, then f ∈ ℌ_σ for σ the Galois representation attached to E; the proof shows S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)}(f) = ⟨ξ, (σ(γ_i))_{i∈I}·x⟩ f. It rests on morphisms (15.1) π^{F,E}_{I,W} : lim_μ H^{0,≤μ,Q̄_ℓ}_{N,I,W} → W_E of sheaves on X^I from the unpublished preprint [BV06] of Braverman–Varshavsky, functorial and Q̄_ℓ-linear in W and compatible with coalescence of legs and with the partial Frobenius — "this last point has not yet been written up". §0.7 explains what this buys: by the examples of Blasius and Lapid for SL_r (r ≥ 3), and of Larsen and S. Wang for other groups including E_8, one representation of the Hecke algebra can occur in several H_σ, and geometric Langlands had been the only systematic way to tell those copies apart.
items.locator: Proposition 15.1 and §15, pp. 173–174, with §§0.7–0.8, pp. 36–37, arXiv v10
items.note: Routed as a source of GS.3 and GS.5 for want of a better home: the atlas has no geometric-Langlands roadmap at all, although `geomlanglands` is one of its galaxy ids. The double conditionality — on the geometric Langlands conjectures and on an unwritten compatibility in [BV06] — must be carried.

items.name: §16: the case of GL_r, and the recursion ingredient of Laurent Lafforgue's proof
items.statement: The chapter, "which brings no new result", shows how Théorème 0.1 gives a new proof of the recursion ingredient (16.4) of [Laf02a] — that to every cuspidal automorphic π of GL_r of level N one can attach a continuous σ : π_1(X ∖ N, η̄) → GL_r(Q̄_ℓ), defined over a finite extension of Q_ℓ, pure of weight 0 and matching π under Satake at every place of X ∖ N — and hence a new proof of the Langlands correspondence for GL_r, once §6.1 and Appendix B of [Laf02a] are added. Remarque 16.1: for GL_r it is enough to prove Proposition 6.2 for V = Λ^k St, k = 1, …, r, which are minuscule, and Proposition 11.7 was already known from Taylor [Tay91]. Lemme 16.2: for σ occurring in (11.11), V irreducible and V_σ = ⊕_τ τ ⊗ 𝔙_τ its decomposition over the irreducible representations τ of π_1(η, η̄), every τ with 𝔙_τ ≠ 0 has τ ⊠ τ^* a subquotient of H_{{1,2},V⊠V^*} — explicitly, for every non-zero h ∈ ℌ_σ, of the finite-dimensional subrepresentation generated by sp^*(C^♯_{δ_V}(h)) — and τ is ι-pure for every ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C. Lemme 16.4: for G = GL_r, assuming the Langlands correspondence known for every GL_{r′} with r′ < r, every σ occurring in the decomposition is irreducible and pure of weight 0 — by Rankin–Selberg [JS81, JPS83], the polynomiality of L(π̌ × π_τ, Z) and the pole of L_S(π̌ × π, Z) at Z = q^{-1} ([Laf02a, Thm. B.10], after Jacquet, Shahidi and Shalika), then ι-purity from Lemme 16.2 and the determinant from class field theory. The proofs are written so as not to use results known as consequences of [Laf02a], to avoid circularity (Remarque 16.3, on [Laf02a, Thm. VII.6]).
items.locator: §16, Remarques 16.1, 16.3, 16.5 and Lemmes 16.2, 16.4, pp. 174–178, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.6 plans Laurent Lafforgue's independent GL_n route, "induction on rank", and "construction in both directions" with the converse theorems [CPS94] and Laumon's product formula [Lau87]; this chapter is exactly the interface between that route and Théorème 11.11, and Lemme 16.2's ι-purity is a GS.5-level statement about the cohomology with two legs.

items.name: Bun_{G,N}: G-bundles on X with level structure, and its rational points
items.statement: The moduli stack Bun_{G,N} of a G-bundle G on X × S with a trivialization over N × S; for a smooth group scheme over X with geometrically connected fibres it is a smooth algebraic stack locally of finite type ([Hei10, prop. 1], [AH13]), and Bun_{G,N}(F_q) is a G(O_N)-torsor over Bun_G(F_q) by Lang’s theorem applied to the Weil restriction G_N. Lemme 12.1 ([Beh91], [Hei10, ex. (1) p. 504], [AH13, prop. 2.2, thm. 2.5]) gives a vector bundle V of rank r with trivialized determinant and a faithful ρ : G → SL(V) with SL(V)/G quasi-affine, so that ρ_* : Bun_G → Bun^0_{GL_r} is representable quasi-affine of finite presentation and the finite-type opens of Bun_G can be pulled back from those of Bun^0_{GL_r} ([Wan11]). The identification Bun_{G,N}(F_q) = G(F)\G(A)/K_N holds for split G, and in general Bun_{G,N}(F_q) is the disjoint union over ker¹(F, G) of the adelic quotients of the pure inner forms (Remarques 8.21, 12.2). The space of cuspidal functions is finite dimensional ([Har74], [BJ79, prop. 5.2]), because cuspidality forces vanishing on very unstable bundles.
items.note: GS.0 plans Bun_G with level structures, the deformation complex, the Harder–Narasimhan bounded opens and the adelic description in the appropriate torsor classes; FA.6 owns the adelic quotient, compact-level functions and the finiteness of cuspidal spaces.

items.name: Perverse sheaves, intersection complexes, universal local acyclicity and relative normalizations
items.statement: The middle perverse t-structure with intermediate extensions; the intersection sheaf IC^E_Y of a stack, normalized to be pure of weight 0, and its renormalization relative to a morphism to a smooth base (here (X ∖ N)^I), which is what makes the coalescence isomorphisms free of shifts and Tate twists; universal local acyclicity relative to X^I; smallness of a proper map and the resulting identification of direct images of intersection complexes; Verdier duality normalized relative to the base; and the constructible A-sheaf conventions of [Del80, §1.1] for A = O_E, E, Q̄_ℓ, with inductive limits treated only as abstract inductive systems except on fibres.
items.locator: §0.12 notations 7), 11), pp. 39–40; used throughout §§1–8, arXiv v10
items.note: EDC.5 plans the perverse t-structure and intermediate extension, EDC.1 Verdier duality, EDC.0 the coefficient, support and geometric-stalk interfaces. The relative-to-the-base normalization used here is a convention the atlas should fix once, since every statement about coalescence depends on it.

items.name: The six operations on stacks with adic coefficients, geometric points and specialization
items.statement: Cohomology of Deligne–Mumford and Artin stacks in the sense of [LMB99] and [LO08]: Rf_!, Rf^!, proper base change and the bounded constructible categories, used to define the cohomology sheaves. Together with the conventions of §8: a geometric point is an algebraically closed field over a point (deliberately *not* the separably closed convention of [SGA4-2-VIII]), Y_{(x)} is the strict localization, a specialization arrow sp : x → y is a morphism Y_{(x)} → Y_{(y)}, and it induces sp^* : F_y → F_x for every constructible sheaf ([SGA4-2-VIII, §7]).
items.locator: §§4.2 and 8, pp. 65 and 106, arXiv v10
items.note: EDC.0 plans the coefficient and geometric-stalk interfaces and SF.1 stack descent, but no stage of the atlas names the Laszlo–Olsson six operations on Artin stacks or the specialization homomorphism of SGA 4; both are used here as black boxes and are worth a maintainer note.

items.name: The Langlands dual group, the L-group and the classical Satake isomorphism
items.statement: Ĝ as a split connected reductive group over Q̄_ℓ (over Z_ℓ in §13) with roots and weights exchanging those of G, the Weyl modules V_λ, the bijection between irreducible representations and dominant coweights, minuscule representations (all weights Weyl-conjugate, equivalently a closed orbit in the affine Grassmannian), and π_1(G) = X_*(T)/X_*(T^{sc}) dual to Z_Ĝ. In the non-split case the L-group ^LG = Ĝ ⋊ Gal(F̃/F) for the pinning-preserving action of the image of Gal(F̄/F) in the automorphisms of the Dynkin diagram, with the local L-groups ^LG_v ⊂ ^LG attached to embeddings F̄ ⊂ F̄_v and unramified over U. The Satake isomorphism [V] ↦ h_{V,v} from the representation ring to the spherical Hecke algebra, in the non-split case in the form S : O(Ĝ_E ⋊ Frob_v//Ĝ_E) ≅ C_c(G(O_v)\G(F_v)/G(O_v), E) of (12.4).
items.note: RG2.5 plans the pinned dual group and the semidirect L-group with its projection and Levi inclusions, FA.6 the unramified Satake dictionary, RG2.3 the parahoric models. The square root of q in E is a coefficient choice, as RG2.5 states.

items.name: Galois and fundamental groups of a function field, Frobenius elements and inertia
items.statement: Gal(F̄/F) = π_1(η, η̄), the fundamental group π_1(U, η̄) of a dense open, the Weil group Weil(η, η̄) = π_1(η, η̄) ×_{Ẑ} Z, the degree homomorphism, the decomposition subgroup Gal(F̄_v/F_v) attached to an embedding F̄ ⊂ F̄_v, the inertia I_v and Frobenius elements Frob_v; the fact that π_1(X ∖ N, η̄) is the topological quotient of π_1(U, η̄) by the closed subgroup generated by the inertia at the missing places, used in Proposition 10.10; and Chebotarev’s theorem, used in Remarques 11.6 and 12.13.
items.note: FA.5 plans Frobenius, Artin factors and Chebotarev over a function field, FA.3 ramification in positive characteristic. The continuity statements of Proposition 10.8(iv) and (C1) are about these topologies.

items.name: The local Langlands parametrization and local–global compatibility (Genestier–Lafforgue)
items.statement: In joint work with Alain Genestier [GL17] the author proves the local Langlands parametrization and its compatibility with the global parametrization of Théorème 11.11; the present paper does not prove it, and states only that it exists. The germ of that work is visible here as Lemme 6.12 and §6.4: the operators S_{V,v} are of local nature at v, proved through the stacks of *restricted* shtukas Cht^{({1},{2}),res(m,n)}_{V⊠V^*} at v (and the local shtukas of (6.24)–(6.26), defined for orientation but not used), whose classifying stacks are quotients of affine Grassmannian data by the groups K_{m,n}; in [GL17] this is extended to all places, including those of N, and to all γ_i in the local Weil group.
items.locator: p. 3 of the introduction; Lemme 6.12 and §6.4, pp. 86–94, arXiv v10
items.note: GS.7 plans exactly this comparison ("At a chosen place compare restriction of the global parameter with the constructed local parameter … Construct local shtuka/uniformization and nearby-cycle comparison maps"). Recorded here so that the atlas knows [GL17] is the source for GS.7, not this paper, and that §6.4 is where the restricted shtukas first appear.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Varshavsky, Moduli spaces of principal F-bundles, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 10 (2004), no. 1, 131–166 [Var04]
prerequisites.why: The foundation: §§2 and 4 of this paper are almost word for word from it. Used items: lemme 2.2 (π_0(Bun_G) ≅ π_1(G)), définition 2.4 and remarque 2.7 c) (the bounded Hecke stacks), lemme 3.1 (algebraicity), lemme A.3 (HN truncations), proposition 2.16 (the geometry of the shtuka stacks), théorème 2.20 and §4 with lemme 4.3 (the étale-local structure), corollaire 2.21, théorème 2.25, lemme A.12.

prerequisites.citation: V. G. Drinfeld, Moduli varieties of F-sheaves, Funktsional. Anal. i Prilozhen. 21 (1987), no. 2, 23–41 (Func. Anal. Appl. 21, 107–122) [Dri87]
prerequisites.why: Shtukas for GL_r with their left/right forms, the smoothness proof generalized by Propositions 2.8–2.9, the partial Frobenius morphisms, and proposition 1.1 (descent of coherent modules along Frobenius), of which Lemme 8.5 is a variant.

prerequisites.citation: V. G. Drinfeld, Langlands' conjecture for GL(2) over functional fields, Proc. ICM (Helsinki 1978), 565–574, Acad. Sci. Fennica, 1980 [Dri78]
prerequisites.why: Théorème 2.1: Drinfeld's lemma for two legs, the key input to Lemme 8.2 and Lemme 8.11; §4.1 introduces the group FGal(F̄^I/F^I) = FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) for ♯I = 2.

prerequisites.citation: V. G. Drinfeld, Cohomology of compactified manifolds of modules of F-sheaves of rank 2, J. Soviet Math. 46 (1989), 1789–1821 [Dri89]
prerequisites.why: Proposition 6.1: the proof of Drinfeld's lemma, generalized here in Lemmes 8.8 and 8.12 (invariant closed subsets of X^I are contained in vertical divisors).

prerequisites.citation: I. Mirković and K. Vilonen, Geometric Langlands duality and representations of algebraic groups over commutative rings, Ann. of Math. 166 (2007), 95–143 [MV07]
prerequisites.why: Geometric Satake with O_E-coefficients (whose argument avoids Verdier duality, which is what makes §13 possible), the modified commutativity constraint introduced before proposition 6.3, lemme 3.9 on the parity of total cohomology, formula (9.9) and the projectives P_Z(ν, A) for the trivial action of the centre, and the smallness of the convolution maps.

prerequisites.citation: D. Gaitsgory, On de Jong's conjecture, Israel J. Math. 157 (2007), 155–191 [Gai07]
prerequisites.why: Théorème 2.6 and appendix B: the form of geometric Satake over X^I that Théorème 1.17 quotes and whose proof it imitates; it proves the stronger statement describing the whole category in terms of Ĝ.

prerequisites.citation: A. Beilinson and V. Drinfeld, Quantization of Hitchin's integrable system and Hecke eigensheaves (1999) [BD99]
prerequisites.why: The Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannian; remarque 2.3.7 and théorème 2.12.1 (gluing G-torsors across the formal neighbourhood, which generalizes Beauville–Laszlo) and the proof of théorème 2.3.4; the pinning of Ĝ that appears in geometric Satake, whence the semidirect L-group.

prerequisites.citation: A. Beauville and Y. Laszlo, Un lemme de descente, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. I Math. 320 (1995), 335–340 [BL95]
prerequisites.why: The descent lemma across a formal neighbourhood, generalized by [BD99, thm. 2.12.1] and used in Construction 1.8.

prerequisites.citation: A. Braverman and Y. Varshavsky, From automorphic sheaves to the cohomology of the moduli spaces of F-bundles, unpublished preprint (2006) [BV06]
prerequisites.why: With [Var04] the source of §4: remarque 2.3.2 gives the coalescence isomorphism (Proposition 4.12), and claim 1.5.5 the local form of the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula (Proposition 6.6); §15 rests on its morphisms (15.1), whose compatibility with the partial Frobenius “has not yet been written up”. The preprint is unpublished, which is a real obstacle for a formalization.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Varshavsky, Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula and a generalization of a theorem of Fujiwara, Geom. Funct. Anal. 17 (2007), no. 1, 271–319 [Var07]
prerequisites.why: 1.2.2, 1.5.7, 2.1.3 and 2.2.4: the formalism of cohomological correspondences and trace maps used throughout §§4 and 6.

prerequisites.citation: R. W. Richardson, Conjugacy classes of n-tuples in Lie algebras and algebraic groups, Duke Math. J. 57 (1988), 1–35 [Ric88]
prerequisites.why: 1.3.2 (coarse quotients and closed orbits), théorème 2.1 (Hilbert–Mumford), théorème 3.6 (semisimple tuples ↔ closed diagonal orbits) = Lemme 11.9, and théorème 5.2 (a Levi of the generated group) = the engine of Lemme 11.10. The whole reconstruction of a Langlands parameter rests on these.

prerequisites.citation: J.-P. Serre, Complète réductibilité, Séminaire Bourbaki 2003/2004, exp. 932, Astérisque 299 (2005), 195–217 [Ser05]
prerequisites.why: G-complete reducibility: the equivalence, in characteristic zero, between semisimplicity of a tuple (every parabolic containing it contains an associated Levi) and reductivity of the Zariski closure of the group it generates; théorème 3.7 recapitulates [Ric88] and [BMR05] for §13.

prerequisites.citation: M. Bate, B. Martin and G. Röhrle, A geometric approach to complete reducibility, Invent. Math. 161 (2005), no. 1, 177–218 [BMR05]
prerequisites.why: Théorème 3.1 completes Richardson's results in characteristic ℓ ≠ 0, and §6 extends complete reducibility to reductive groups that need not be connected: the two inputs that make the F̄_ℓ-coefficient Théorème 13.2 possible.

prerequisites.citation: C. Procesi, The invariant theory of n × n matrices, Adv. Math. 19 (1976), 306–381 [Pro76]
prerequisites.why: The invariant theory of tuples of matrices in characteristic zero, and the fact that Θ_1(χ_{St}) determines all the Θ_n for GL_r (Remarque 11.8).

prerequisites.citation: R. Taylor, Galois representations associated to Siegel modular forms of low weight, Duke Math. J. 63 (1991), 281–332 [Tay91]
prerequisites.why: Every pseudo-character over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is the character of a semisimple r-dimensional representation: Proposition 11.7 for H = GL_r (Remarque 11.8).

prerequisites.citation: D. Hilbert, Über die vollen Invariantensysteme, Math. Ann. 42 (1893), no. 3, 313–373 [Hil1893]
prerequisites.why: Finite generation of the algebra of diagonal-conjugation invariants O((Ĝ_E)^n//Ĝ_E) (Notation 11.1), which is what makes the coarse quotient a scheme of finite type.

prerequisites.citation: D. Mumford, J. Fogarty and F. Kirwan, Geometric Invariant Theory, 3rd ed., Ergeb. Math. Grenzgeb. 34, Springer, 1994 [MFK94]
prerequisites.why: §I.2 for coarse quotients and finite generation (Notation 11.1) and §I.1 for the Reynolds operator, used in the continuity step of Proposition 11.7.

prerequisites.citation: H. Poincaré, Sur les groupes des équations linéaires, Acta Math. 4 (1884), 201–312 [Poi1884]
prerequisites.why: §0.9: the idea of characterizing conjugacy classes of monodromy representations by finitely many numerical invariants, the ancestor of the excursion operators.

prerequisites.citation: H. Jacquet, R. P. Langlands and the Langlands programme: R. P. Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, Lecture Notes in Math. 170 (1970), 18–61 [Lan70]
prerequisites.why: The global Langlands correspondence whose “automorphic to Galois” direction is proved here.

prerequisites.citation: A. Borel, Automorphic L-functions, in Automorphic forms, representations and L-functions (Corvallis), Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 33, part 2, AMS, 1979, 27–61 [Bor79]
prerequisites.why: The L-group as a semidirect product Ĝ ⋊ Gal(F̃/F) for a pinning-preserving action, §2.5 for the “trivial” functoriality ^LΥ used in Proposition 12.5, and §I.3 with lemme 3.5 for the parabolic subgroups of Richardson type in §13.

prerequisites.citation: I. Satake, Theory of spherical functions on reductive algebraic groups over p-adic fields, Publ. Math. IHÉS 18 (1963), 5–69 [Sat63]
prerequisites.why: The classical Satake isomorphism, which the decomposition is compatible with; with [Car79], [Gro98, prop. 3.6] (the h_{V,v} are a basis over Z[q^{1/2}, q^{-1/2}]) and [BR94] for the non-split form (12.4).

prerequisites.citation: L. Lafforgue, Chtoucas de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands, Invent. Math. 147 (2002), no. 1, 1–241 [Laf02a]
prerequisites.why: The full GL_r correspondence, obtained by a completely different, trace-formula method. §16 shows how Théorème 0.1 reproves its recursion ingredient; théorème B.10, théorème VII.6, lemme VI.13 and §II.1.a are quoted, and §6.1 with appendix B carry the induction on r.

prerequisites.citation: J. W. Cogdell and I. I. Piatetski-Shapiro, Converse theorems for GL_n, Publ. Math. IHÉS 79 (1994), 157–214 [CPS94]
prerequisites.why: The converse theorems that, with Laumon's product formula, give the “Galois to automorphic” direction for GL_r by induction (§16 and p. 3).

prerequisites.citation: G. Laumon, Transformation de Fourier, constantes d'équations fonctionnelles et conjecture de Weil, Publ. Math. IHÉS 65 (1987), 131–210 [Lau87]
prerequisites.why: The product formula for epsilon factors, the other half of the induction for GL_r (§16).

prerequisites.citation: E. Lau, On generalised D-shtukas, Dissertation, Bonn 2004, Bonner Math. Schriften 369 [Lau04]
prerequisites.why: Théorème 8.1.4: Drinfeld's lemma in general (unpublished); lemme 8.1.2 (descent of étale coverings along Frobenius); lemme 9.2.1 (a partial-Frobenius-invariant strict closed subset of X^I lies in a union of vertical divisors, and the Zariski density of the Frobenius orbit of ∆(η)) — used in Lemme 8.12 and Propositions 8.31–8.32.

prerequisites.citation: C. Xue, Cohomologie cuspidale des champs de chtoucas, thèse de doctorat, Université Paris-Saclay (2017) [Xue17]
prerequisites.why: Finite dimensionality of H_{I,W}, which this paper deliberately avoids using (Remarques 0.27, 8.29, 9.5), and a general framework for the parabolic-induction correspondences defining cuspidality in the non-split case.

prerequisites.citation: A. Genestier and V. Lafforgue, Chtoucas restreints pour les groupes réductifs et paramétrisation de Langlands locale, arXiv:1709.00978 (2017) [GL17]
prerequisites.why: The companion paper: the local Langlands parametrization and local–global compatibility, and the general form of Lemme 6.12 (the excursion operators are of local nature at v). Restricted shtukas, sketched here in §6.4, are its main tool.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Laszlo and M. Olsson, The six operations for sheaves on Artin stacks I, II, Publ. Math. IHÉS 107 (2008), 109–168 and 169–210 [LO08]
prerequisites.why: With [LMB99] (Laumon–Moret-Bailly, Champs algébriques), the ℓ-adic formalism on the Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type used to define the cohomology sheaves (Definition 4.1).

prerequisites.citation: X. Zhu, The geometric Satake correspondence for ramified groups, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 48 (2015), no. 2, 409–451 [Zhu15]
prerequisites.why: With [Ric14] (T. Richarz, A new approach to the geometric Satake equivalence, Doc. Math. 19 (2014), 209–246), the twisted geometric Satake equivalence that Théorème 12.16 quotes for the non-split case.

prerequisites.citation: J. Heinloth, Uniformization of G-bundles, Math. Ann. 347 (2010), no. 3, 499–528 [Hei10]
prerequisites.why: Proposition 1: Bun_G is a smooth algebraic stack locally of finite type for a smooth group scheme over the curve, and example (1) p. 504 for Lemme 12.1; with [Beh91], [AH13] (Arasteh Rad–Hartl, arXiv:1302.6351, props. 2.2, 2.5, thm. 3.14) and [Wan11] for the finite-type truncations.

prerequisites.citation: F. Bruhat and J. Tits, Groupes réductifs sur un corps local II. Schémas en groupes, Publ. Math. IHÉS 60 (1984), 197–376 [BT84]
prerequisites.why: §§5.1.9 and 4.6: the parahoric integral models used to build the smooth group scheme over X in the non-split case (§12.1).

prerequisites.citation: D. Kazhdan, An introduction to Drinfeld's Shtuka, in Automorphic forms, representations and L-functions, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 33, part 2, AMS, 1979, 347–356 [Kaz79]
prerequisites.why: Théorème 7: the group W̃_Λ, another description of FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) for two legs (Remarque 8.18).
