routes.reason:
This paper is the roadmap's own named source: GS.0's source route reads “V. Lafforgue global bundle/level setup”, GS.1's “V. Lafforgue geometric Satake input”, GS.2's “V. Lafforgue shtuka construction”, GS.3's “V. Lafforgue Hecke-finite cohomology construction”, GS.4's “V. Lafforgue Drinfeld-lemma and coalescence arguments” and GS.5's “V. Lafforgue arXiv:1209.5352: general reductive automorphic-to-Galois theorem”. Every item in this route is therefore **planned**, not missing, and the route exists to pin the source: it gives each stage the exact statement, hypotheses and locator it has to reproduce, in the same way PAPER-FENG-24 routes its §§2 and 5.1 to GS.1/GS.2/GS.4/GS.5. The correspondence is stage by stage:
- **GS.0** — Bun_{G,N} with level structure, the Harder–Narasimhan truncations Cht^{≤μ}, the lattice Ξ and the finite-type quotients; and, for non-split G, the description of Bun_{G,N}(F_q) as the disjoint union over ker¹(F, G) of adelic quotients for inner forms (Remarques 8.21, 12.2), which is exactly GS.0's instruction not to identify the whole stack with one double quotient.
- **GS.1** — the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian with its Beauville–Laszlo description, the closed strata Gr_{I,W}, the Weil-restriction groups G_{Σn_ix_i}, the smallness of the forgetful maps, and Théorème 1.17 — one direction of geometric Satake, stated as a functor over X^I with the four properties a)–d), the modified commutativity constraint and half-integral Tate twists. Théorème 12.16 is the twisted variant needed for non-split G.
- **GS.2** — Définitions 0.2 and 0.6 (multi-leg shtukas as successive modifications with an isomorphism to the Frobenius pullback), the bound on relative positions imposed as an inverse image, Proposition 2.8 (the local model map is smooth of dimension (Σn_i)dim G) and Lemme 12.19.
- **GS.3** — H^{0,≤μ,E}_{N,I,W} and the functor W ↦ H (Définitions 0.4, 0.11), the Hecke operators as sheaf morphisms, the Hecke-finite sector with Proposition 8.27, the spaces H_{I,W} and Proposition 9.7, and Proposition 8.23 (cuspidal = Hecke-finite), which is GS.3's acceptance test.
- **GS.4** — the partial Frobenius morphisms, the coalescence isomorphisms χ_ζ, the creation/annihilation morphisms, Drinfeld's lemma (Lemme 0.18), the group FWeil(η^I, η̄^I) with the factorization of its action, and Corollaire 8.34 (specialization is an isomorphism on Hecke-finite parts).
- **GS.5** — the excursion operators, their relations (Lemme 10.1, Proposition 10.8), the algebra B and its spectral decomposition, Lemmes 10.2/10.4 identifying unramified Hecke operators as excursion operators, Proposition 10.10, Proposition 11.7 (reconstruction of σ) and Théorèmes 11.11 and 12.3.
- **GS.6** — §16, the comparison with Laurent Lafforgue's theorem for GL_r, including Lemme 16.4's induction on the rank through the converse theorems and Laumon's product formula.
- **GS.7** — the companion paper [GL17] with Genestier is the source of the local parametrization and of local–global compatibility; this paper only states that it exists, and the route records that so GS.7 does not expect it here.
Two boundaries matter. First, the excursion formalism of §§9–10 is also planned, for the Fargues–Scholze **local** setting, in ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES0 and LanglandsParameterStacks LP2; those stages own W_E for a local field, finite wild ramification and Bun_G on the Fargues–Fontaine curve, whereas everything here is global over a curve, so the two must cite each other and not be proved twice. Second, this paper proves only the automorphic-to-Galois direction and no multiplicity formula, which is precisely GS.5's stated acceptance boundary.

Four things in the paper are in the direction of these stages but are not planned by any of them.
- **The Eichler–Shimura relations (Proposition 7.1).** No stage of the atlas states an Eichler–Shimura relation for shtukas, yet the whole of §8 rests on it: it is what makes the Hecke-finite part a union of constructible subsheaves stable under the partial Frobenius (Proposition 8.27), hence what makes GS.3's “required finiteness” of the Hecke-finite sector and GS.4's application of Drinfeld's lemma possible. It needs the extension of the Hecke operators to all of (X ∖ N)^I (Corollaire 6.5), and its proof is a Cayley–Hamilton-style tensor identity using only Λ^{dim V+1}V = 0. PAPER-FENG-24 cites the same relation, in Cong Xue's form, as an input to its Part II; planning it once here serves both.
- **The F_ℓ-coefficient decomposition (§13).** Proposition 13.1 and Théorème 13.2 give the same canonical decomposition for C^{cusp}_c(…, F̄_ℓ) indexed by continuous semisimple σ : Gal(F̄/F) → Ĝ(F̄_ℓ), with Ĝ over Z_ℓ. GS.5 says nothing about modular coefficients and GS.1 explicitly defers them (“integral and modular Satake are further coefficient branches”), which this chapter requires. Remarque 13.3 must be carried with it: unlike Théorème 11.11, H_σ is probably not contained in a Hecke eigenspace, because mod-ℓ Hecke operators need not be diagonalizable — so GS.5's “unramified Satake compatibility” is weaker in this branch.
- **The two conjectures of §12.2 (12.7 and 12.12).** That the parameters occurring come from elliptic Arthur parameters, and that the decomposition is defined over Q, indexed by motivic parameters and independent of ℓ. These are recorded as a register of what is expected but unproved, which is the honest complement to GS.5's acceptance boundary (“The output does not assert every parameter occurs, packet multiplicities, or a full general-group inverse correspondence”). The Part II GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur proposed by PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26 is where Arthur-type weight constraints are being planned, and its design job should cross-reference Conjecture 12.7 rather than restate it.
- **The link with geometric Langlands (§15).** The atlas has no geometric-Langlands roadmap at all, although `geomlanglands` is one of its galaxy ids; §15 is two pages relating the cohomology of the shtuka stacks to Hecke eigensheaves, with Proposition 15.1 explicitly “conditional on a result not yet written up”, and §0.7 explains that geometric Langlands was until then the only systematic way to separate the copies of one automorphic representation sitting in different H_σ (the Blasius–Lapid examples for SL_r, r ≥ 3, and Larsen's and S. Wang's for other groups including E_8). It is routed here with its conditional status attached rather than made into a roadmap of its own on the strength of two pages.

LP2 constructs the excursion algebra Exc(W, Ĝ) from finite free-group cocycle invariants, the affine coarse quotient and “the relation to closed semisimple geometric orbits”, and LP2:semisimple-characters proves Fargues–Scholze VIII.3.8, that excursion characters determine a unique conjugacy class of continuous semisimple L-parameters; LP3 does the integral reductive invariant theory those statements need. What none of them states is the characteristic-zero invariant theory that the argument actually turns on, and which this paper isolates: an n-tuple (g_1, …, g_n) ∈ H(Q̄_ℓ)^n is semisimple (every parabolic containing it contains an associated Levi containing it, equivalently its generated subgroup has reductive Zariski closure, [Ser05]) if and only if its diagonal conjugation orbit is closed, by Richardson [Ric88, Thm. 3.6] — Lemme 11.9 here — so that the Q̄_ℓ-points of the coarse quotient H^n//H are exactly the conjugacy classes of semisimple tuples; together with [Ric88, Thm. 5.2], that a tuple lying over the same point as a semisimple one has a Levi isomorphic to the latter's generated subgroup. Proposition 11.7 then reconstructs σ from a compatible system Θ_n of algebra morphisms on O(H^n//H) for a **profinite** group and an H that need not be connected, with the maximality hypotheses (H1) on dim⟨g_1, …, g_n⟩ and (H2) on the centralizer, the uniqueness Lemme 11.10, the verification that σ is a homomorphism and the two surjectivity arguments that give its continuity. The GL_r shadow is Remarque 11.8: Θ_1(Tr) together with Λ^{r+1}St = 0 is a pseudo-character and Taylor [Tay91] reconstructs σ — the string “pseudo-character” does not occur anywhere in the atlas. Remarque 11.2 names [Pro76, Ric88, Vin96] for these quotients and §0.9 traces the idea to Poincaré [Poi1884], with Hilbert [Hil1893] for finite generation. Plan it once here, in characteristic zero for a profinite group and a possibly disconnected reductive H, and let both LP2:semisimple-characters and GS.5 import it.

MP.4 constructs the adelic metaplectic cover and the global Weil representation, for the classical metaplectic group. §14 indicates how the whole method of this paper adapts to metaplectic covers of a reductive group over a function field: the cover is encoded as a μ_N-gerbe over Bun_G which, by Remarque 14.1, is a factorization gerbe in the sense of [GL16] and is defined over F_q because N divides q − 1; the metaplectic geometric Satake equivalence of Lysenko replaces Théorème 1.17; and one obtains a decomposition of the cuspidal automorphic forms of the cover indexed by parameters valued in the metaplectic dual group. Neither factorization gerbes nor metaplectic geometric Satake appear anywhere in the atlas, and MP.0–MP.8 are written for the symplectic/Heisenberg cover over a number field, so this is a genuine addition in MP.4's direction. The route must carry the paper's own status: the chapter is titled “Indications”, the constructions are sketched rather than proved here, and Remarque 14.2 says only that one may hope the F_ℓ-coefficient results of §13 extend to the metaplectic case. Plan it as a programme with Lysenko's papers as the sources, not as a theorem of this paper.
